chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v01] Now, for its practical use, the sacrifice is first explained. In that context, initiation alone becomes the means for both enjoyment and liberation.

[tal-a15-v10] It is clearly said there, in the knowledge section, in the discussion of the principles according to cause and effect and what is to be rejected or accepted.

[tal-a15-v02] This works either by itself or through consecration, and its auxiliary aspect is now shown. Whoever desires enjoyments in a particular domain is appointed right there.

[tal-a15-v03] In the revered Svayambhuva scripture the Lord says that one attains success through mantra power. According to fitness, wherever a person's inclination lies, there he is placed.

[tal-a15-v04] He should be appointed so that he does not fall away. Thus, in the revered Malinimata, the teacher declared initiation to be a means for enjoyment and more, not for enjoyment alone.

[tal-a15-v05] Without initiation there is no eligibility for Shaiva yoga. And initiation does not bring about only eligibility for yoga.

[tal-a15-v06] Through Shiva initiation one also gains eligibility for mantra and liberation. Thus, in this statement of the Malini, initiation is taught as a direct means to liberation.

[tal-a15-v07] Earlier texts have spoken of initiation, and it is also said that, through consecration passed down in succession, initiation becomes a means to both liberation and enjoyment.

[tal-a15-v08] For those who are determined but, due to incapacity, cannot take up knowledge, the teacher has declared this easier means as their procedure.

[tal-a15-v09] Thus it is declared in the revered Matanga scripture as a means to liberation. For knowledge, whose nature is right understanding, is directly liberating.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-:C15 atha śrītantrāloke pañcadaśamāhnikam athaitadupayogāya yāgastāvannirūpyate / tatra dīkṣaiva bhoge ca muktau cāyātyupāyatām svayaṃ saṃskārayogādvā tadaṅgaṃ tatpradarśyate / yo yatrābhilaṣedbhogān sa tatraiva niyojitaḥ siddhibhāṅmantraśaktyeti śrīmatsvāyaṃbhuve vibhuḥ / yogyatāvaśato yatra vāsanā yasya tatra saḥ yojyo na cyavate tasmāditi śrīmālinīmate / vadanbhogādyupāyatvaṃ dīkṣāyāḥ prāha no guruḥ na cādhikāritā dīkṣāṃ vinā yoge@sti śāṅkare / na ca yogādhikāritvamekamevānayā bhavet api mantrādhikāritvaṃ muktiśca śivadīkṣayā / ityasminmālinīvākye sākṣānmokṣābhyupāyatā dīkṣāyāḥ kathitā prācyagranthena punarucyate / pāramparyeṇa saṃskṛtyā mokṣabhogābhyupāyatā yeṣāmadhyavasāyo@sti na vidyāṃ pratyaśaktitaḥ / sukhopāyamidaṃ teṣāṃ vidhānamuditaṃ guroḥ iti śrīmanmataṅgākhye hyuktā mokṣābhyupāyatā / samyagjñānasvabhāvā hi vidyā sākṣādvimocikā uktaṃ tatraiva tattvānāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvataḥ / heyādeyatvakathane vidyāpāda iti sphuṭam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v11] But for those who are incapable, initiation, conduct, and absorption are prescribed, and these should be preceded by knowledge. Therefore the knower is the most supreme.

[tal-a15-v12] Knowledge comes from scripture, and scripture is not to be heard by one who is uninitiated. Therefore initiation serves for him only as the consecration that makes this possible.

[tal-a15-v13] Wherever the teacher appoints him, he attains a fruit suited to his own understanding. This, it is said, was declared earlier regarding the knower.

[tal-a15-v14] But if, by the Lord's grace, some divine fitness arises in both teacher and disciple, then initiation is of no use to them.

[tal-a15-v15] Then knowledge itself is initiation, as explained in the revered Traisika. And for him there suddenly arises knowledge of the meaning of all the scriptures.

[tal-a15-v16] Thus, according to the teaching of the revered Malini, one who possesses innate awareness is the highest-qualified. Indeed, such a knower is regarded as a teacher.

[tal-a15-v17] Seeking benefit for himself or for others, he should contemplate this. By that statement in the Malini scripture, all of this has been made clear.

[tal-a15-v18] Thus, in the injunction of the revered Kairana scripture, some are said to be fit for knowledge, others for conduct, others for initiation, and others for yoga.

[tal-a15-v19] There, the one who has the stated marks, is skilled in action, yoga, and knowledge, and is elevated through successively higher levels, is declared to be the teacher.

[tal-a15-v20] And that teacher, having examined or questioned the disciple who has been purified by the descent of any one of the powers mentioned before, should perform the rite of initiation.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tatrāśaktāstu ye teṣāṃ dīkṣācaryāsamādhayaḥ / te vidyāpūrvakā yasmāttasmājjñānyuttamottamaḥ jñānaṃ ca śāstrāttaccāpi śrāvyo nādīkṣito yataḥ / ato@sya saṃskriyāmātropayogo dīkṣayā kṛtaḥ yatra tatrāstu guruṇā yojito@sau phalaṃ punaḥ / svavijñānocitaṃ yāti jñānītyuktaṃ purā kila yasya tvīśaprasādena divyā kācana yogyatā / guroḥ śiśośca tau naiva prati dīkṣopayogitā jñānameva tadā dīkṣā śrītraiśikanirūpaṇāt / sarvaśāstrārthavettṛtvamakasmāccāsya jāyate iti śrīmālinīnītyā yaḥ sāṃsiddhikasaṃvidaḥ / sa uttamādhikārī syājjñānavānhi gururmataḥ ātmane vā parebhyo vā hitārthī cetayedidam / ityuktyā mālinīśāstre tatsarvaṃ prakaṭīkṛtam jñānayogyāstathā keciccaryāyogyāstathāpare / dīkṣāyogyā yogayogyā iti śrīkairaṇe vidhau tatroktalakṣaṇaḥ karmayogajñānaviśāradaḥ / uttarottaratābhūmyutkṛṣṭo gururudīritaḥ sa ca prāguktaśaktyanyatamapātapavitritam / parīkṣya pṛṣṭvā vā śiṣyaṃ dīkṣākarma samācaret

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v21] And it is said in the Svacchanda scripture that the teacher himself should ask the disciple: what fruit do you seek? I will begin the means suited to that.

[tal-a15-v22] Because inclinations differ, attainment of the goal is impelled by mantra. In the offering, mantra, seal, path, and substances have a common use.

[tal-a15-v23] Because inclinations differ, the fruits of disciples and of the teacher differ. The Shaiva practitioner is twofold: one whose way of life abandons worldly concerns.

[tal-a15-v24] One type follows worldly duty, desires fruit, abides in what is good, and avoids what is evil. The seeker of liberation is twofold: the seedless one is free from pledges and the like.

[tal-a15-v25] Another kind of candidate is like a child, a fool, an old person, a woman, an enjoyer, or someone sick. For such a person, the teaching of Shiva prescribes the seeded initiation.

[tal-a15-v26] But for those who can endure the pairs of opposites, there is a seeded initiation made of pledges that confers grace. They must observe it, and they must also keep the special pledges.

[tal-a15-v27] For a desireless seeker of liberation, one should clearly contemplate the non-existence of past and future actions. But one should not do anything to remove the action that has already begun.

[tal-a15-v28] But for a practitioner who seeks power, one should purify in just that way. This initiation, grounded in Shiva-duty, takes away worldly duty.

[tal-a15-v29] For those who remain in worldly duty, this initiation purifies only what is unrighteous, not what is auspicious. It is an initiation without mantra worship.

[tal-a15-v30] When the body formed by already-begun karma falls away, this person enjoys powers such as aṇimā. After enjoying them, he goes onward to the level where he becomes joined, whether in the sakala state or in a limited condition.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-uktaṃ svacchandaśāstre ca śiṣyaṃ pṛcchedguruḥ svayam / phalaṃ prārthayase yādṛktādṛksādhanamārabhe vāsanābhedataḥ sādhyaprāptirmantrapracoditā / mantramudrādhvadravyāṇāṃ home sādhāraṇā sthitiḥ vāsanābhedato bhinnaṃ śiṣyāṇāṃ ca guroḥ phalam / sādhako dvividhaḥ śaivadharmā lokojjhitasthitiḥ lokadharmī phalākāṃkṣī śubhasthaścāśubhojjhitaḥ / dvidhā mumukṣurnirbījaḥ samayādivivarjitaḥ bālabāliśavṛddhastrībhogabhugvyādhitādikaḥ / anyaḥ sabījo yasyetthaṃ dīkṣoktā śivaśāsane vidvaddvandvasahānāṃ tu sabījā samayātmikā / dīkṣānugrāhikā pālyā viśeṣasamayāstu taiḥ abhāvaṃ bhāvayetsamyakkarmaṇāṃ prācyabhāvinām / mumukṣornirapekṣasya prārabdhrekaṃ na śādhayet sādhakasya tu bhūtyarthamitthameva viśodhayet / śivadharmiṇyasau dīkṣā lokadharmāpahāriṇī adharmarūpiṇāmeva na śubhānāṃ tu śodhanam / lokadharmiṇyasau dīkṣā mantrārādhanavarjitā prārabdhadehabhede tu bhuṅkte@sāvaṇimādikam / bhuktvordhvaṃ yāti yatraiṣa yukto@tha sakale@kale

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v31] In the seedless initiation, one should purify the bond of pledge-conduct. Liberation can come through initiation alone, together with constant devotion to God and to the guru.

[tal-a15-v32] This seedless initiation is said to give immediate liberation, because it cuts away the three bonds of past, future, and already-begun karma.

[tal-a15-v33] If a purified person gives up the body at the end of initiation, he reaches the supreme state. But if the body is given up in the case of seeded initiation, the result fails because karma is absent.

[tal-a15-v34] The initiated person must always guard the bond of pledge-conduct. The guru himself should first ask, understand, and carefully examine the candidate.

[tal-a15-v35] When the guru wishes to give the right initiation, he should rely on the candidate's corresponding disposition. If the descent of grace has come to someone, the initiating guru, with regard to that initiation,

[tal-a15-v36] must not show disrespect. This is established as the command of Shambhu. If the person is poor, the guru himself should perform the initiation using his own wealth.

[tal-a15-v37] A disciple may even beg for initiation with nothing more than durva grass and water. Or the disciple may first give to the guru wealth that is his own or that he has obtained by begging.

[tal-a15-v38] By giving it, that wealth becomes purified and fit to be offered. In this matter, the first requirement is the entry into the freedom of the state of Shiva.

[tal-a15-v39] That person alone should be made the guru, for he is capable of giving initiation. His entry into the state of Shiva has been shown to come about through many means.

[tal-a15-v40] One gradual path takes an external form, using bathing, placement, worship, and similar acts. Among these many practices, one establishes the state of Shiva in the heart.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-samayācārapāśaṃ tu nirbījāyāṃ viśodhayet / dīkṣāmātreṇa muktiḥ syādbhaktyā deve gurau sadā sadyonirvāṇadā seyaṃ nirbījā yeti bhaṇyate / atītānāgatārabdhapāśatrayaviyojikā dīkṣāvasāne śuddhasya dehatyāge paraṃ padam / dehatyāge sabījāyāṃ karmābhāvādvipadyate samayācārapāśaṃ tu dīkṣitaḥ pālayetsadā / evaṃ pṛṣṭvā parijñāya vicārya ca guruḥ svayam ucitāṃ saṃvidhitsustāṃ vāsanāṃ tādṛśīṃ śrayet / āyātaśaktipātasya dīkṣāṃ prati na daiśikaḥ avajñāṃ vidadhīteti śaṃbhunājñā nirūpitā / svadhanena daridrasya kuryāddīkṣāṃ guruḥ svayam api dūrvāmbubhiryadvā dīkṣāyai bhikṣate śiśuḥ / bhikṣopāttaṃ nijaṃ vātha dhanaṃ prāggurave śiśuḥ dadyādyena viśuddhaṃ tadyāgayogyatvamaśnute / tatrādau śivatāpattisvātantryāveśa eva yaḥ sa eva hi guruḥ kāryastato@sau dīkṣaṇe kṣamaḥ / śivatāveśitā cāsya bahūpāyā pradarśitā kramikā bāhyarūpā tu snānanyāsārcanādibhiḥ / bahvīṣu tāsu tāsveṣa kriyāsu śivatāṃ hṛdi

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v41] By firmly establishing it, the clear-minded practitioner attains the state of Shiva. Having become Shiva, he undertakes to do whatever he wishes.

[tal-a15-v42] An external means identified with Shiva is not by itself what gives liberation. Liberation comes when teacher and disciple firmly hold the recognition: this is Shiva; I am indeed Shiva.

[tal-a15-v43] For the two of them, firm identification, understood as cause and its bearer, is what liberates. The external does not succeed without the inner, and the inner does not succeed when cut off from the external.

[tal-a15-v44] Success comes through knowledge and action together, and this paired principle shines forth. He established this by citing the revered Brahmayamala, where it says, 'O God...'

[tal-a15-v45] And in the revered Ananda scripture it is said that the wise person has no impurity. Rather, bathing and wearing good clothes serve to produce contentment.

[tal-a15-v46] There, through the familiar sequence of purifying the body and related measures, those who bathe can enter inwardly without effort. From that, purity arises.

[tal-a15-v47] The bathing of the God of Gods is connected with what is called his eight forms. In that context, the true immersion is the inward plunging into the burning of impurity lit by mantra.

[tal-a15-v48] There, centered in the heart of the chosen mantra, one should go and return three steps within the space of cow dust and perform the earthly bath. That bath gives steadiness.

[tal-a15-v49] Having removed impurity with clay consecrated by the weapon mantra, one should then wash the body in order from head to feet with waters consecrated by the five-limb mantras.

[tal-a15-v50] One should immerse while reciting the root mantra together with its limbs, or through becoming one with it. After rising, one should contemplate in the sky the sun that contains all the luminous deities.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-saṃdadhaddṛḍhamabhyeti śivabhāvaṃ prasannadhīḥ / śivībhūto yadyadicchettattatkartuṃ samīhate śivābhimānitopāyo bāhyo heturna mokṣadaḥ / śivo@yaṃ śiva evāsmītyevamācāryaśiṣyayoḥ hetutadvattayā dārḍhyābhimāno mocako hyaṇoḥ / nādhyātmena vinā bāhyaṃ nādhyātmaṃ bāhyavarjitam siddhyejjñānakriyābhyāṃ taddvitīyaṃ saṃprakāśate / śrībrahmayāmale deva iti tena nyarūpayat śrīmadānandaśāstre ca nāśuddhiḥ syādvipaścitaḥ / kintu snānaṃ suvastratvaṃ tuṣṭisaṃjananaṃ bhavet tatra prasiddhadehādimātṛnirmalatākramāt / ayatnato@ntarantaḥ syānnairmalya snāyatāṃ tataḥ snānaṃ ca devadevasya yanmūrtyaṣṭakamucyate / tatraivaṃ mantradīpte@ntarmaladāhe nimajjanam tatreṣṭamantrahṛdayo gorajo@ntaḥ padatrayam / gatvāgatya bhajetsnānaṃ pārthivaṃ dhṛtidāyakam astramantritamṛddhūtamalaḥ pañcāṅgamantritaiḥ / jalairmūrdhādipādāntaṃ kramādākṣālayettataḥ nimajjetsāṅgamūlākhyaṃ japannā tanmayatvataḥ / utthāyāśeṣasajjyotirdevatāgarbhamambare

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v51] With water and the Malini mantra, one should satisfy the sun, the satisfier of the whole world, and also satisfy the gods, ancestors, sages, yakshas, demons, and whatever else is elemental.

[tal-a15-v52] One should satisfy all beings through the vital breath, whose nature is power, and that power is the sun. Then one should recite the single supreme mantra according to the method of utterance taught earlier.

[tal-a15-v53] This is regarded as the water bath, culminating in the awareness of becoming one with that. For the fire bath, ash arisen from fire is recited over with the weapon mantra so that it removes impurity.

[tal-a15-v54] Ash consecrated with the five-limb mantras is applied to the head, face, heart, and secret place. Then a handful of ash, recited over with the root mantra and its limbs, should be cast on the head.

[tal-a15-v55] After washing the hands and feet with water alone, one performs sipping and the other acts, then satisfaction and recitation. In this way, the ash bath is indeed the fiery bath.

[tal-a15-v56] When a refreshing wind blows gently, like the dust raised by cows, one should perform the wind bath by uttering the mantra, or by moving back and forth in that wind.

[tal-a15-v57] When one sits in the stainless sky with a gaze made one-pointed on the pervasive expanse, remembering the mantra, what other purity could there be beyond that?

[tal-a15-v58] Or, if one lets water falling from the stainless sky touch the body while joined with mantra recitation, that is such a sky bath.

[tal-a15-v59] Thus, by contemplating with the state of Shiva in the lights of moon, sun, and fire, and by immersing purified through the Malini, where would one not become fit?

[tal-a15-v60] The self alone is the supreme lord, the great pool beyond ritual observance. Having immersed the universe there, one should abide in that very place as pure and as the purifier.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sūryaṃ jalena mālinyā tarpayedviśvatarpakam / devānpitṝnmunīnyakṣān rakṣāṃsyanyacca bhautikam sarvaṃ saṃtarpayetprāṇo vīryātmā sa ca bhāskaraḥ / tato japetparāmekāṃ prāguktoccārayogataḥ ā tanmayatvasaṃvitterjalasnānamidaṃ matam / agnyutthaṃ bhasma śastreṇa japtvā malanivarhaṇam kavaktrahṛdguhyapade pañcāṅgairbhasma mantritam / bhasmamuṣṭiṃ sāṅgamūlajaptāṃ mūrdhni kṣipettataḥ hastapādau jalenaiva prakṣālyācamanādikam / tarpaṇaṃ japa ityevaṃ bhasmasnānaṃ hi taijasam gorajovatyanudrikte vāyau hlādini mantravāk / gatyāgatiprayoge vā vāyavyaṃ snānamācaret amale gagane vyāpinyekāgrībhūtadṛṣṭikaḥ / smaranmantraṃ yadāsīta kānyā nirmalatā tataḥ yadi vā nirmalādvyomnaḥ patatā vāriṇā tanum / sparśayenmantrajapayuṅ nābhasaṃ snānamīdṛśam evaṃ somārkatejaḥsu śivabhāvena bhāvanāt / nimajjandhautamālinyaḥ kva vā yogyo na jāyate ātmaiva parameśāno nirācāramahāhradaḥ / viśvaṃ nimajjya tatraiva tiṣṭhecchuddhaśca śodhakaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v61] Thus there is the group of eight baths, each later one better than the previous in purification. In every case, afterward one should apply that mantra in a unified form.

[tal-a15-v62] The sage devoted to the eight baths attains in order firmness, nourishment, the burning away of impurity, power, pervasion, purification, abiding, and non-difference.

[tal-a15-v63] These eight forms are indeed gracious in nature and are essentially Shiva. Through meditation on them as one's own form and as Shiva's form, they grant their respective fruits.

[tal-a15-v64] By this method in worship, performing the application beginning with the bulb and the support, whether in expanded or condensed form, one obtains the corresponding fruit beginning with earth.

[tal-a15-v65] For in the movement of yoga, the mantras are earthly on earth, watery in water, and so on, until in Shiva they become wholly of Shiva's nature.

[tal-a15-v66] In the revered Nirmaryada scripture this is well explained: earth and the other elements also have a special form approved by heroic practitioners.

[tal-a15-v67] For heroic practitioners, battle dust is the heroic water, there is heroic ash and the great wind, and also the cremation ground, forest, and sky, along with the moon and sun as brought into that setting.

[tal-a15-v68] The self, well established with all the affliction of conceptual thought shaken off, completes the heroic group of eight forms to be honored in bathing, worship, and so on.

[tal-a15-v69] In the revered Mantrishiras it is taught that one may use wine, liquor, or other such spirits, provided they are very tasty, clear, subtle, and very fragrant.

[tal-a15-v70] Using the substance as present in the bulb and so on, within and without, one performs the five consecrations: inspection, sprinkling, striking, nourishing, and veiling.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-iti snānāṣṭakaṃ śuddhāvuttarottaramuttamam / sarvatra paścāttaṃ mantramekībhūtamupāharet ghṛtyāpyāyamalaploṣavīryavyāptimṛjisthitīḥ / abhedaṃ ca kramādeti snānāṣṭakaparo muniḥ etā hyanugrahātmāno mūrtayo@ṣṭau śivātmikāḥ / svarūpaśivarūpābhyāṃ dhyānāttattatphalapradāḥ anena vidhinārcāyāṃ kandādhārādiyojanām / kurvanvyāsasamāsābhyāṃ dharādestatphalaṃ bhajet tathāhi yogasaṃcāre mantrāḥ syurbhuvi pārthivāḥ / āpye āpyā yāvadamī śive śivamayā iti śrīnirmaryādaśāstre@pi taditthaṃ sunirūpitam / dharādeśca viśeṣo@sti vīrasādhakasaṃmataḥ raṇareṇurvīrajalaṃ vīrabhasma mahāmarut / śmaśānāraṇyagaganaṃ candrārkau tadupāhitau ātmā nirdhūtaniḥśeṣavikalpātaṅkasusthitaḥ / snānārcādāvityupāsyaṃ vīrāṇāṃ vigrahāṣṭakam śrīmantriśirasi proktaṃ madyaśīdhusurādinā / susvādunā prasannena tanunā susugandhinā kandalādigatenāntarbahiḥ saṃskārapañcakam / kṛtvā nirīkṣaṇaṃ prokṣya tāḍanāpyāyaguṇṭhanam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v71] In the middle of the mantra circle one performs worship and satisfaction with drops. With that substance one sprinkles oneself and performs consecratory sprinkling using the jar seal.

[tal-a15-v72] Through satisfaction of the deity, resting on the path of both body and vital breath, one obtains the fruit of all pilgrimages, austerities, sacrifices, gifts, and the like.

[tal-a15-v73] In the wine bath, the foremost practitioner who seeks liberation may become liberated, because wine is of the nature of Śiva and all mantras arise from Śiva.

[tal-a15-v74] There is no difference between Śiva and Śakti; the rays arise from Śakti, and wine produces their bliss. Therefore wine is of the nature of Śiva.

[tal-a15-v75] When the full form of consciousness is awakened, one is fit for ritual action. Bathing distinguished by mantra, meditation, and absorption is real bathing; what lacks that is not.

[tal-a15-v76] Bathing is fitting because it brings fitness for nyāsa and other rites. This eightfold bathing is twofold, as outer and inner.

[tal-a15-v77] The inner bath is the flooding of nectar from the upper moon, established above the cranial aperture and pervading a span of one and a half finger-widths.

[tal-a15-v78] Eight forms are taught, each arising from the dvādaśānta. One may perform any one of these baths, or do them in two, three, or more ways.

[tal-a15-v79] Thus the rule of bathing has been declared by Bhairava for purification. Now what must be done after bathing is taught.

[tal-a15-v80] Seeing that one's inner state is clear, one should then go to the place of worship, such as a mountain top, a riverbank, a solitary liṅga, and so on.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-mantracakrasya tanmadhye pūjāṃ vipruṭpratarpaṇam / tenātmasekaḥ kalaśamudrayā cābhiṣecanam devatātarpaṇaṃ dehaprāṇobhayapathāśritam / sarvatīrthatapoyajñadānādi phalamaśnute madyasnāne sādhakendro mumukṣuḥ kevalībhavet / yataḥ śivamayaṃ madyaṃ sarve mantrāḥ śivodbhavāḥ śivaśaktyorna bhedo@sti śaktyutthāstu marīcayaḥ / tāsāmānandajanakaṃ madyaṃ śivamayaṃ tataḥ prabuddhe saṃvidaḥ pūrṇe rūpe@dhikṛtibhājanam / mantradhyānasamādhānabhedātsnānaṃ tu yanna tat yuktaṃ snānaṃ yato nyāsakarmādau yogyatāvaham / asya snānāṣṭakasyāsti bāhyāntaratayā dvitā āntaraṃ tadyathordhvendudhārāmṛtapariplavaḥ / yato randhrordhvagāḥ sārdhamaṅgulaṃ vyāpya saṃsthitāḥ mūrtayo@ṣṭāvapi proktāḥ pratyekaṃ dvādaśāntataḥ / eṣāmekatamaṃ snānaṃ kuryāddvitryādiśo@pivā iti snānavidhiḥ prokto bhairaveṇāmalīkṛtau / snānānantarakartavyamathedamupadiśyate bhāvaṃ prasannamālocya vrajedyāgagṛhaṃ tataḥ / parvatāgranadītīraikaliṅgādi yaducyate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v81] Those outer places are for particular attainments, not for liberation. The inner mountain-top and the like are within the body, approached through the application of prāṇa.

[tal-a15-v82] For practitioners this is a means to attainment, not to liberation. The pīṭha-place, however, is always fit for worship, as the scriptures declare.

[tal-a15-v83] That pīṭha, in its outer and inner form, is clearly present outside and in the body, because the Supreme Lord set it forth in the revered Naiśa Sañcāra.

[tal-a15-v84] His will is the supporting pīṭha in which all that moves and does not move is situated. That foremost pīṭha is Kāmarūpa, and from it comes the pair of bindu and nāda.

[tal-a15-v85] The nāda-pīṭha is Pūrṇagiri on the right, and on the left is the pīṭha Uḍḍayana. With bindu as the chief, this is the triad of pīṭhas.

[tal-a15-v86] One should know the half-pīṭha as having the form of conceptualization. Beyond that, in the śākta domain, Kuṇḍalinī and Vedakala belong to the triad of upapīṭhas.

[tal-a15-v87] Devīkoṭṭa and Ujjayinī are two, and Kulagiri is another; Lālana, Baindava, and Vyāpti form the triad of saṃdohakas.

[tal-a15-v88] With Puṇḍravardhana, Vārendra, and likewise Ekāmra on the outside, the pīṭha is declared ninefold in an inner-outer sequence.

[tal-a15-v89] Those who know the kṣetras speak of an eightfold group corresponding to the eight petals of the heart-lotus: Prayāga, Varaṇā, then Aṭṭahāsa, and Jayantikā.

[tal-a15-v90] Vārāṇasī, Kāliṅga, Kulūtā, and likewise Lāhulā belong to the eight upakṣetras, which they say correspond to the eight front petals of the heart-lotus.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tadbāhyamiha tatsiddhiviśeṣāya na muktaye / ābhyantaraṃ nagāgrādi dehāntaḥ prāṇayojanam sādhakānāmupāyaḥ syātsiddhaye natu muktaye / pīṭhasthānaṃ sadā yāgayogyaṃ śāstreṣu bhaṇyate tacca bāhyāntarādrūpādbahirdehe ca susphuṭam / yataḥ śrīnaiśasañcāre parameśo nyarūpayat tasyecchā pīṭhamādhāro yatrasthaṃ sacarācaram / agryaṃ tatkāmarūpaṃ syādbindunādadvayaṃ tataḥ nādapīṭhaṃ pūrṇagirirdakṣiṇe vāmataḥ punaḥ / pīṭhamuḍḍayanaṃ bindurmukhyaṃ pīṭhatrayaṃ tvidam jñeyaṃ saṃkalpanārūpamardhapīṭhamataḥ param / śāktaṃ kuṇḍalinī vedakalaṃ ca tryupapīṭhakam devīkoṭṭojjayinyau dve tathā kulagiriḥ paraḥ / lālanaṃ baindavaṃ vyāptiriti saṃdohakatrayam puṇḍravardhanavārendre tathaikāmramidaṃ bahiḥ / navadhā kathitaṃ pīṭhamantarbāhyakrameṇa tat kṣetrāṣṭakaṃ kṣetravido hṛdambhojadalāṣṭakam / prayāgo varaṇā paścādaṭṭahāso jayantikā vārāṇasī ca kāliṅgaṃ kulūtā lāhulā tathā / upakṣetrāṣṭakaṃ prāhurhṛtpadmāgradalāṣṭakam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v100] Likewise, even one situated in a sacred seat attains fitness for knowledge, yoga, and the rest, primarily for one who sees inwardly in the body, in the breath, and in consciousness.

[tal-a15-v91] Viraja and Airuḍikā, Hālā, Elā, Pūḥ, Kṣīrikā, Purī, the place called Māyā, and Marudeśa are understood in both outer and inner form.

[tal-a15-v92] The eight upasaṃdohakas correspond to the junctions of the heart-lotus petals: Jālandhara, Naipāla, Kaśmīra, Gargikā, and Hara.

[tal-a15-v93] There is also the site at the gate of the mleccha direction, Kurukṣetra, and Kheṭaka. A two-path junction arises, a three-path junction from the meeting of two, and further from the meeting of three.

[tal-a15-v94] They hold that the four-path junction arises there itself by dissolution in the Śakti-bearing principle, and in this body it is established in the region of the nose, palate, and aperture.

[tal-a15-v95] The middle triad is said to be the middle of the brows, the throat, and the heart. The navel, the bulb, and the abode of great bliss form the kaula triad.

[tal-a15-v96] Mountain tops, riverbanks, and solitary liṅgas—why say more? All of that is in consciousness and present in prāṇa.

[tal-a15-v97] Therefore worship should be situated in the body, taking the body as its abode. External worship, however, is for those who are skilled in the corresponding inner yoga path.

[tal-a15-v98] The goddesses arise from their own nature, and the sacred seat is said to be external to that. This is like barbarians who, by their own nature, follow the path of unrighteousness.

[tal-a15-v99] In some such place, knowledge and yoga may be established by fixed rule, yet even one who is made of consciousness can fall into sinfulness through association with those there.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-virajairuḍikā hālā elā pūḥ kṣīrikā purī / māyākhyā marudeśaśca bāhyābhyantararūpataḥ hṛtpadmadalasandhīnāmupasaṃdohakāṣṭatā / jālandharaṃ ca naipālaṃ kaśmīrā gargikā haraḥ mlecchadigdvāravṛttiśca kurukṣetraṃ ca kheṭakam / dvipathaṃ dvayasaṃghaṭṭāttripathaṃ trayamelakāt catuṣpathaṃ śaktimato layāttatraiva manvate / nāsāntatālurandhrāntametaddehe vyavasthitam bhrūmadhyakaṇṭhahṛtsaṃjñaṃ madhyamaṃ tadudāhṛtam / nābhikandamahānandadhāma tatkaulikaṃ trayam parvatāgraṃ nadītīramekaliṅgaṃ tadeva ca / kiṃ vātibahunā sarvaṃ saṃvittau prāṇagaṃ tataḥ tato dehasthitaṃ tasmāddehāyatanago bhavet / bāhye tu tādṛśāntaḥsthayogamārgaviśāradāḥ devyaḥ svabhāvājjāyante pīṭhaṃ tadvāhyamucyate / yathā svabhāvato mlecchā adharmapathavartinaḥ tatra deśe niyatyetthaṃ jñānayogau sthitau kvacit / yathācātanmayo@pyeti pāpitāṃ taiḥ samāgamāt tathā pīṭhasthito@pyeti jñānayogādipātratām / mukhyatvena śarīre@ntaḥ prāṇe saṃvidi paśyataḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v101] This whole universe is already here, so what is the use of other outward displays of wandering? Thus, for those who seek the fruit of each respective circle, the matter applies both inwardly and outwardly.

[tal-a15-v102] The difference of sacred places is varied and, in scripture, beyond counting. In the Vīrāvalihṛdaya, seven places are mentioned, along with a pair of śakti-lotuses.

[tal-a15-v103] Places such as the path of the gods, a crossroads, a cremation ground, a solitary spot, and an empty tree are taught as sites to be understood through etymology, quality, condition, and figurative meaning.

[tal-a15-v104] Worship for liberation may take place in a circle established there, in the body, or externally; therefore no essential difference in the worship is to be made on the basis of place.

[tal-a15-v105] This attainment does not operate by means of place, because it comes from the clarity of one's inner state; this is also said in the revered Nishacara for those who seek accomplishment.

[tal-a15-v106] One who seeks liberation should cast off attachment to place like a snake sheds its skin, because liberation is not produced by place; it comes when the truth reaches one's hearing.

[tal-a15-v107] When the truth of the guru is heard, liberation comes; worship then serves to strengthen it. Wherever the heart-lotus opens, that is where this awakening takes place.

[tal-a15-v108] In that very inner abode, the glory of both outer and inner worship is established. Liberation does not come from going somewhere else; it comes from cutting the knot of ignorance.

[tal-a15-v109] Through the expansion of awareness in the glorious line of heroes, a pure mind directed toward the guru becomes the cause for either liberation or attainment.

[tal-a15-v110] In both liberation and attainment, whatever is pleasing to the mind and fit for worship can be the cause, because its effectiveness comes from the completeness of conditions operating through necessity.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-viśvametatkimanyaiḥ syādbahirbhramaṇaḍambaraiḥ / ityevamantarbāhye ca tattaccakraphalārthinām sthānabhedo vicitraśca sa śāstre saṃkhyayojjhitaḥ / śrīvīrāvalihṛdaye sapta sthānāni śaktikamalayugam surapathacatuṣpathākhyaśmaśānamekāntaśūnyavṛkṣau ca / iti nirvacanaguṇasthityupacāradṛśā vibodha evoktaḥ tadadhiṣṭhite ca cakre śārīre bahiratho bhavedyāgaḥ / muktaye tanna yāgasya sthānabhedaḥ prakalpyate deśopāyā na sā yasmātsā hi bhāvaprasādataḥ / uktaṃ ca śrīniśācāre siddhisādhanakāṅkṣiṇām sthānaṃ mumukṣuṇā tyājyaṃ sarpakañcukavattvidam / muktirna sthānajanitā yadā śrotrapathaṃ gatam gurostattvaṃ tadā muktistaddārḍhyāya tu pūjanam / yatra yatra hṛdambhojaṃ vikāsaṃ pratipadyate tatraiva dhāmni bāhye@ntaryāgaśrīḥ pratitiṣṭhati / nānyatragatyā mokṣo@sti so@jñānagranthikartanāt tacca saṃvidvikāsena śrīmadvīrāvalīpade / guravastu vimuktau vā siddhau vā vimalā matiḥ heturityubhayatrāpi yāgauko yanmanoramam / niyatiprāṇatāyogātsāmagrītastu yadyapi

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v111] Although attainments and purity of being may both arise, a person whose heart has become pure reflects on whatever is best of all in that situation.

[tal-a15-v112] What one seeks becomes fruitful through firmness, and the Sāraśāstra says that the one who is free of conceptual construction truly succeeds.

[tal-a15-v113] Those who remain caught in conceptual construction struggle even when they perform what the ritual prescribes, but when that underlying power is truly accessed, the mantras rise clearly and effectively.

[tal-a15-v114] Statements from the Spanda and others make this same point clear: in worship, recitation, and absorption, the same principle holds whether one seeks attainment or liberation.

[tal-a15-v115] Wherever the heart comes to rest in a beautiful stillness, that place is fit for worship; having reached it, a purified practitioner may remain outwardly engaged while grounded there.

[tal-a15-v116] For the establishment of outer worship, one should perform a general nyāsa using the Mātṛkā, the Mālinī, or both, either in sequence or in non-sequence.

[tal-a15-v117] Using the two modes of emission and withdrawal, one should place the elements one by one and in pairs on the forehead, face, eyes, ears, nose, cheeks, teeth, and lips.

[tal-a15-v118] In this stage, sixteen phonemes ending with visarga are placed in pairs, including on the crown-tuft and tongue, while the ka and ca groups are assigned to the right and left shoulders, arms, hands, fingers, and nails.

[tal-a15-v119] One should place the ṭa and ta groups in order on the hips, thighs, and so forth, and place the pa group on the sides, back, belly, and heart, making a ninefold assignment.

[tal-a15-v120] This completes the Mātṛkā nyāsa, extending through the bodily constituents from skin to seed, and now the Mālinī nyāsa is explained.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-siddhayo bhāvavaimalyaṃ tathāpi nikhilottamam / vimalībhūtahṛdayo yattatra pratibimbayet sādhyaṃ tadasya dārḍhyena saphalatvāya kalpate / uktaṃ śrīsāraśāstre ca nirvikalpo hi sidhyati kliśyante savikalpāstu kalpokte@pi kṛte sati / tadākramya balaṃ mantrā ayamevodayaḥ sphuṭaḥ ityādibhiḥ spandavākyairetadeva nirūpitam / tasmātsiddhyai vimuktyai vā pūjājapasamādhiṣu tatsthānaṃ yatra viśrāntisundaraṃ hṛdayaṃ bhavet / yāgaukaḥ prāpya śuddhātmā bahireva vyavasthitaḥ nyāsaṃ sāmānyataḥ kuryādbahiryāgaprasiddhaye / mātṛkāṃ mālinīṃ vātha dvitayaṃ vā kramākramāt sṛṣṭyapyayadvayaiḥ kuryādekaikaṃ saṃghaśo dviśaḥ / lalāṭavaktre dṛkkarṇanāsāgaṇḍaradauṣṭhage dvaye dvaye śikhājihve visargāntāstu ṣoḍaśa / dakṣānyayoḥ skandhabāhukarāṅgulinakhe kacau vargau ṭatau kramātkaṭyāmūrvādiṣu niyojayet / pavargaṃ pārśvayoḥ pṛṣṭhe jaṭhare hṛdyatho nava tvagraktamāṃsasūtrāsthivasāśukrapurogamān / ityeṣa mātṛkānyāso mālinyāstu nirūpyate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v121] Place na, ṛ, ṝ, ḷ, and ḹ on the crest and the garland of the head, and tha on the crown. Assign the eyes above and below, place ī on the nose, ṇu and ṇū on the two seals, and place the corresponding letters on the two ears.

[tal-a15-v122] Place the ba-ka group with i and ā in order on the mouth, teeth, tongue, and palate. Place va, bha, and ya on the throat and the right and left shoulders, and place ḍa and ḍha on the two arms.

[tal-a15-v123] Place ṭha on the two hands, jha and ña on the branches, and jra and ṭa on the trident and skull. Place pa on the heart and cha and la on the two breasts. Mā, associated with milk, and sa joined with visarga are said to be the life-breath.

[tal-a15-v124] Ha is declared to be the vital breath. Ṣa and kṣa go to the belly and the navel. The group ending with ma goes to the hips, the private parts, and the pair of thighs, and likewise to the two knees.

[tal-a15-v125] Place e and ai, and the pair that follows them, on the two shins, and place da and pha on the two feet. This is the goddess Mālinī, because she is stirred into activity by the possessor of power.

[tal-a15-v126] Because it enters into ritual efficacy, that body is, in ultimate truth, a body of Śakti. It arises from the mutual stirring of the seeds and wombs, through an emissive arising.

[tal-a15-v127] What accomplishment would she not grant, or what deficiency would she not fill? Although the intermixture of wombs, seeds, and phonemes exists in many forms, her power is complete.

[tal-a15-v128] Even so, the sequence beginning with na and ending with pha is proclaimed as the primary one. By uttering from pha to na, the whole circle of the path is formed.

[tal-a15-v129] When withdrawn into consciousness, she is full and complete, so how could she truly be described by words? For that reason the scriptures speak of her in many ways, through forms such as kula, puttalika, and others.

[tal-a15-v130] Although she is sung in many divisions, this Malini, beginning with na and ending with pha, is the primary one. She is the inner, uncontracted form of Bhairava, who is the mass of sound.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-na śikhā ṛ ṝ ḷ ḷḷ ca śiromālā tha mastakam / netrāṇi cordhve dho@nye ī ghrāṇaṃ mudre ṇu ṇū śrutī bakavarga+i+ā vaktradantajihvāgiri kramāt / vabhayāḥ kaṇṭhadakṣādiskandhayorbhujayorḍaḍhau ṭho hastayorjhañau śākhā jraṭau śūlakapālake / pa hṛcchalau stanau kṣīramā sa jīvo visargayuk prāṇo havarṇaḥ kathitaḥ ṣakṣāvudaranābhigau / maśāntā kaṭiguhyoruyugmagā jānunī tathā eaikārau tatparau tu jaṅghe caraṇagau daphau / ityeṣā mālinī devī śaktimatkṣobhitā yataḥ kṛtyāveśāttataḥ śāktī tanuḥ sā paramārthataḥ / anyonyaṃ bījayonīnāṃ kṣobhādvaisargikodayāt kāṃ kāṃ siddhiṃ na vitaretkiṃ vā nyūnaṃ na pūrayet / yonibījārṇasāṃkaryaṃ bahudhā yadyapi sthitam tathāpi nādiphānto@yaṃ kramo mukhyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ / phakārādisamuccārānnakārānte@dhvamaṇḍalam saṃhṛtya saṃvidyā pūrṇā sā śabdairvarṇyate katham / ataḥ śāstreṣu bahudhā kulaputtalikādibhiḥ bhedairgītā hi mukhyeyaṃ nādiphānteti mālinī / śabdarāśerbhairavasya yānucchūnatayāntarī

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v131] She is like a mother because she brings forth what is to come, and so she is called the mother. As Malini, garlanded and upheld by the Rudras, she supports both accomplishment and liberation.

[tal-a15-v132] She flowers in fruits and is worthy of worship, like a six-footed bee in the sound of withdrawal. Because of ra and la, she is endowed with powers of withdrawal, giving, taking, and more.

[tal-a15-v133] Śambhunātha declared that this sound-array Mālinī is of the nature of Śiva and Śakti, remembered as one.

[tal-a15-v134] Because each is full by Śiva-Śakti nature, this restores what is lost in rite, power, or form.

[tal-a15-v135] Mantras that are placed are filled by replacement and give that fruit, as said in Śrīpūrvatantra, even without special rite.

[tal-a15-v136] For the purpose of the desire-active body, Mālinī is placed; this qualifier is determined as cause and cause-meaning, though the source differs.

[tal-a15-v137] This was spoken here for accomplishing the desired fruit: even mantras with collyrium, Garuḍa and others, are not supreme.

[tal-a15-v138] Filled by Mālinī, they accomplish by strength; but for liberation, even one desiring fruit places another mantra here as Mālinī.

[tal-a15-v139] Place after reciting, and recite without effort for release; thus place Mātṛkā or Mālinī in order, both.

[tal-a15-v140] According to accomplishment or liberation, letters are placed; both simultaneously use akṣa-hrīṃ and napha-hrīṃ, masses of union and separation.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sā māteva bhaviṣyattvāttenāsau mātṛkoditā / mālinī mālitā rudrairdhārikā siddhimokṣayoḥ phaleṣu puṣpitā pūjyā saṃhāradhvaniṣaṭpadī / saṃhāradānādānādiśaktiyuktā yato ralau ekatvena smarantīti śaṃbhunātho nirūcivān / śabdarāśirmālinī ca śivaśaktyātmakaṃ tvidam ekaikatrāpi pūrṇatvācchivaśaktisvabhāvatā / tena bhraṣṭe vidhau vīrye svarūpe vānayā param mantrā nyastāḥ punarnyāsātpūryante tatphalapradāḥ / uktaṃ śrīpūrvatantre ca viśeṣavidhihīnite nyasyecchāktaśarīrārthaṃ bhinnayoni tu mālinīm / viśeṣaṇamidaṃ hetau hetvarthaśca nirūpitaḥ yatheṣṭaphalasiddhyai cetyatraivedamabhāṣata / sāñjanā api ye mantrā gāruḍādyā na te param mālinyā pūritāḥ sidhdyai balādeva tu muktaye / tasmātphalepsurapyanya mantraṃ nyasyātra mālinīm nyasyejjaptvāpica japedayatnādapavṛktaye / ityevaṃ mātṛkāṃ nyasyenmālinīṃ vā kramāddvayam siddhimuktyanusārādvā varṇānvā yugapaddvayoḥ / akṣahrīṃ naphahrīmetau piṇḍau saṃghāvihānayoḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v141] The expressive ones are placement; when placement is done by these two, it is single or with limb-body-Brahma, or its reverse.

[tal-a15-v142] In collective placement, the two masses are separate; they are placed in order or without order, then place only one and join.

[tal-a15-v143] One desiring accomplishment by rite should perform more rite; even one not desiring receives that rite for more of his own fruit.

[tal-a15-v144] One desiring accomplishment by meditation and recitation should do rite for purification by his own will, then more according to prior rule.

[tal-a15-v145] The aspirant for liberation should perform for him as desired; the attainment of Shiva-nature is indeed the purpose of these nyasa and related rites.

[tal-a15-v146] Having thus performed nyasa in the argha vessel, one should perform the rite according to the stated rule; thereafter worship with the installed mantras.

[tal-a15-v147] Because all beings attain perfection from Shiva, and from the full one comes non-difference of agents in this worship.

[tal-a15-v148] The whole host of agents is shown as non-different from Shiva; in the example of worship one attains all, even going and the rest.

[tal-a15-v149] As a horse that has come under the rider's control through the bridle's freedom, though mounted in battle, does not transgress that training.

[tal-a15-v150] So the agent habituated by worship-practice and made Shiva-like, though going or standing, abandons duality of agents.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-vācakau nyāsa etābhyāṃ kṛte nyāse@thavaikakaḥ / eṣa cāṅgatanubrahmayukto vā tadviparyayaḥ sāmudāyikavinyāse pṛthak piṇḍāvimau kramāt / akramādathavā nyasyedekamevātha yojayet kriyayā siddhikāmo yaḥ sa kriyāṃ bhūyasīṃ caret / anīpsurapi yastasmai bhūyase svaphalāya sā yastu dhyānajapābhyāsaiḥ siddhīpsuḥ sa kriyāṃ param / saṃskṛtyai svecchayā kuryāt prāṅnayenātha bhūyasīm mumukṣuratha tasmai vā yathābhīṣṭaṃ samācaret / śivatāpattirevārtho hyeṣāṃ nyāsādikarmaṇām evaṃ nyāsaṃ vidhāyārghapātre vidhimupācaret / uktanītyaiva tatpaścāt pūjayennyastavācakaiḥ yataḥ samastabhāvānāṃ śivātsiddhimayādatho / pūrṇādavyatirekitvaṃ kārakāṇāmihārcayā samastaṃ kārakavrātaṃ śivābhinnaṃ pradarśitam / pūjodāharaṇe sarvaṃ vyaśnute gamanādyapi yathāhi vāhakaṭakabhramasvātantryamāgataḥ / aśvaḥ saṃgrāmarūḍho@pi tāṃ śikṣāṃ nātivartate tathārcanakriyābhyāsaśivībhāvitakārakaḥ / gacchaṃstiṣṭhannapi dvaitaṃ kārakāṇāṃ vyapojjhati

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v151] Thus for one established in unity-practice, this universe suddenly, by force, like a dancer, may flash as full Shiva-nature.

[tal-a15-v152] Our supreme guru said in the praise of worship: 'Ah, what sweet taste, what festival of Shiva-worship!'

[tal-a15-v153] The agitation of thirty-six principles, where it shines, is for full Shiva-entry into the universe; those who worship.

[tal-a15-v154] They are Shiva indeed; what fruit for the full ones? Even without knowledge and yoga, action like nyasa and worship.

[tal-a15-v155] Thus by granting unity-samapatti, bestowing other fruit, the practitioner too has attained mantra-unity with that good vipra.

[tal-a15-v156] The universe would quickly attain unobstructedness and its own perfection; it is said by the Supreme Lord: neither rule nor worship procedure.

[tal-a15-v157] Only through remembrance is success desired; thus ritual action gives absorption in that, because of this.

[tal-a15-v158] Through unity of all agents, her supreme body becomes identity with the support of the sacrificer by the order of place-purification rite.

[tal-a15-v159] By nyāsa order, the sacrificer, offering, support, instruments, gifts, and transmissions attain identity with Śiva-ness.

[tal-a15-v160] The argha vessel is the recipient, therefore it is taken; whatever water and instruments are situated in it serve purification or worship.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tathaikyābhyāsaniṣṭhasyākramādviśvamidaṃ haṭhāt / saṃpūrṇaśivatākṣobhanarīnartadiva sphuret uvāca pūjanastotre hyasmākaṃ paramo guruḥ / aho svādurasaḥ ko@pi śivapūjāmayotsavaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśato@pi tattvānāṃ kṣobho yatrollasatyalam / tadetādṛkpūrṇaśivaviśvāveśāya ye@rcanam kurvanti te śivā eva tānpūrṇānprati kiṃ phalam / vināpi jñānayogābhyāṃ kriyā nyāsārcanādikā itthamaikyasamāpattidānātparaphalapradā / sādhakasyāpi tatsadvipradamantraikatāṃ gatam viśvaṃ vrajadavighnatvaṃ svāṃ siddhiṃ śīghramāvahet / uktaṃ ca parameśena na vidhirnārcanakramaḥ kevalaṃ smaraṇātsiddhirvāñchiteti matādiṣu / tadevaṃ tanmayībhāvadāyinyarcākriyā yataḥ samastakārakaikātmyaṃ tenāsyāḥ paramaṃ vapuḥ / yaṣṭrādhārasya tādātmyaṃ sthānaśuddhividhikramāt yaṣṭṛyājyatadādhārakaraṇādānasaṃpradāḥ / nyāsakrameṇa śivatātādātmyamadhiśerate arghapātramapādānaṃ tasmādādīyate yataḥ / yacca tatsthaṃ jalādyetatkaraṇaṃ śodhane@rcane

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v161] All touched by drops from the argha vessel becomes pure; other purity will arise from contact with Śiva-sun rays.

[tal-a15-v162] The Lord said in the holy former scripture: in that argha-vessel rite, one should not provide any unpurified thing at all.

[tal-a15-v163] Therefore all is pure, even what is impure; that is pure, and impurity is to be known from the intention of binding the paśu.

[tal-a15-v164] From one's own state or from what was previously provided, therefore whatever is present here is by the grace of consciousness.

[tal-a15-v165] However much that is extremely suitable in this sacrifice, like a living being, by this method of reasoning when existence is far from knowledge.

[tal-a15-v166] When consciousness arises, then there one should declare suitability or unsuitability; for heroes indeed here, mutually, the nectar of one's own image.

[tal-a15-v167] Entered into each sacrifice rite, self-realized gurus raise up consciousness that is submerged; but that is well.

[tal-a15-v168] For worship, suitable bliss arises because consciousness rises up; therefore it submerges the predominance of non-conscious body and the like.

[tal-a15-v169] Whatever produces bliss, is fit for worship, and captivates the heart is therefore praised in the teachings of Kula, Krama, the transcendent Trika essence, and others.

[tal-a15-v170] Wine, kādambarī, śīdhu, and such substances have supreme greatness, yet in the teaching meant for bound souls they are restricted in order to maintain worldly order.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-arghapātrāmbuvipruḍbhiḥ spṛṣṭaṃ sarvaṃ hi śudhyati / śivārkakarasaṃsparśātkānyā śuddhirbhaviṣyati ūce śrīpūrvaśāstre tadarghapātravidhau vibhuḥ / na cāsaṃśodhitaṃ vastu kiṃcidapyupakalpayet tena śuddhaṃ tu sarvaṃ yadaśuddhamapi tacchuci / aśuddhatā ca vijñeyā paśutacchāsanāśayāt svatādavasthyātpūrvasmādathavāpyupakalpitāt / tena yadyadihāsannaṃ saṃvidaścidanugrahāt kiyato@pi tadatyantaṃ yogyaṃ yāge@tra jīvavat / anena nayayogena yadāsattividūrate saṃvideti tadā tatra yogyāyogyatvamādiśet / vīrāṇāmata eveha mithaḥ svapratimāmṛtam tattadyāgavidhāviṣṭaṃ gurubhirbhāvitātmabhiḥ / unmajjayati nirmagnāṃ saṃvidaṃ yattu suṣṭhu tat arcāyai yogyamānando yasmādunmagnatā citaḥ / tenācidrūpadehādiprādhānyavinimajjakam ānandajananaṃ pūjāyogyaṃ hṛdayahāri yat / ataḥ kulakramottīrṇatrikasāramatādiṣu madyakādambarīśīdhudravyādermahimā param / lokasthitiṃ racayituṃ madyādeḥ paśuśāsane

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v171] In that teaching it is declared impure, yet in some contexts there is purity; for example, the five cow products are purifying, as are soma remains and ritual vessels.

[tal-a15-v172] There are rules such as the concluding bath, holding the black antelope horn in the hand, not performing the sacrifice without the wife, and treating all deities as equal.

[tal-a15-v173] Even in the scriptures meant for bound souls, the great lord showed a liquor offering in a brahma session and an offering of omentum, intestine, and heart.

[tal-a15-v174] In opposed judgments, one says the goose is to be eaten and another says it is not; amid such confusion, clarity is like a lamp shining at midnight in terrible snowy darkness.

[tal-a15-v175] Among smārta teachings, the one principle that prevails is purification through non-difference from Śiva; for ignorance, mere appeal to the Veda, attachment, aversion, and such defects undermine authority.

[tal-a15-v176] These defects can uproot the authority of the sages' own words; even in the Veda, what is said not to be eaten is taught elsewhere as something to be eaten.

[tal-a15-v177] Injunction and prohibition do not rest on one single basis; if in a particular context something is not to be eaten, then that is how it stands there, and the matter is resolved accordingly.

[tal-a15-v178] Thus, because their domains differ, Vedic revelation does not override the word of Śiva; only if their domains were the same would there be a relation of overruling and being overruled.

[tal-a15-v179] If their domains were equal, Vedic revelation itself would be overruled; this has already been established. Now we return to the present topic: after performing installation on the body and the offering vessel.

[tal-a15-v180] After sprinkling all the worship implements with drops of water from the common offering vessel, one should then perform the external worship.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-proktā hyaśuddhistatraiva tasya kvāpi viśuddhatā / pañcagavye pavitratvaṃ somacarṇanapātrayoḥ vidhiścāvabhṛthasnānaṃ haste kṛṣṇaviṣāṇitā / na patnyā ca vinā yāgaḥ sarvadaivatatulyatā surāhutirbrahmasatre vapāntrahṛdayāhutiḥ / pāśaveṣvapi śāstreṣu tadadarśi maheśinā ghorāndhyahaimananiśāmadhyagāciradīptivat / bhakṣyo haṃso na bhakṣyo@sāviti ripratipattiṣu smārtīṣu vijayatyeko yaḥ śivābhedaśuddhikaḥ / ajñatvavedādarśitvarāgadveṣādayo hyamī munīnāṃ vacasi svasminprāmāṇyonmūlanakṣamāḥ / vede@pi yadabhakṣyaṃ tadbhakṣyamityupadiśyate na vidhipratiṣedhākhyadharmayorekamāspadam / atha tatra na tadbhakṣyaṃ tadā tena tathā tataḥ evaṃ viṣayabhedānno śivokterbādhikā śrutiḥ / kvacidviṣayatulyatvādbādhyabādhakatā yadi tadbādhyā śrutireveti prāgevaitannirūpitam / prakṛtaṃ brūmahe kṛtvā nyāsaṃ dehārghapātrayoḥ sāmānyamarghapātrāmbhovipruḍbhiḥ prokṣya cākhilam / yāgopakaraṇaṃ paścādbāhyayāgaṃ samācaret

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v181] In a circle of light, in space, or on a well-smeared ground, one should worship the mothers, who stand on the trident, the sun, the bull, and Nandin, and also worship the lord of the field.

[tal-a15-v182] One should also worship the yoginīs, either with separate mantras joined with oṃ, namas, and their names, or with a single utterance, as they are called the outer retinue.

[tal-a15-v183] In worship the mantra is oṃ, the name in the fourth-case form, and namas. Having thus worshipped outside, one should sprinkle the doorway and then worship it.

[tal-a15-v184] This procedure is seen in the teaching of the Three-headed One and others. Above the doorway one should worship Gaṇeśa and Lakṣmī, on the right and left, and then continue with those associated with them.

[tal-a15-v185] In the middle one should place Vāgīśvarī, and likewise the pair Diṇḍi and Mahodara, in order on their own right and left, following that same sequence.

[tal-a15-v186] One should properly worship each one: Nandi and Kāla, the river who flows by three paths, Kālindī, and the goat-faced and ram-faced pair, on the door branches beginning from one's own right.

[tal-a15-v187] Below the threshold one should worship Dehalī, Ananta, Īśa, and the supporting power; in the middle of the doorway one should worship the great weapon together with Sarasvatī.

[tal-a15-v188] All these, situated on the lotus support, are declared to be destroyers of obstacles. In their worship the mantra is used as before, with an arrangement of two lamps.

[tal-a15-v189] One should perform the worship here with offering water, flowers, touch, incense, food offerings, and homage; and the offering water should be prepared with excellent substances.

[tal-a15-v190] Or one may perform the worship of the doorway deities with a single utterance. If one performs secret worship, then that outer retinue is included in that condensed form.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-prabhāmaṇḍalake khe vā suliptāyāṃ ca vā bhuvi / triśūlārkavṛṣāndikasthā mātaraḥ kṣetrapaṃ yajet yoginīśca pṛthaṅmantrairoṃnamonāmayojitaiḥ / ekoccāreṇa vā bāhyaparivāretiśabditāḥ tāro nāma caturthyantaṃ namaścetyarcane manuḥ / evaṃ bahiḥ pūjayitvā dvāraṃ prokṣya prapūjayet triśiraḥśāsanādau ca sa dṛṣṭo vidhirucyate / gaṇeśalakṣmyau dvārordhve dakṣe vāme tayoḥ punaḥ madhye vāgīśvarīṃ diṇḍimahodarayugaṃ tathā / kramātsvadakṣavāmasthaṃ tathaitena krameṇa ca ekaikaṃ pūjayetsamyaṅ nandikālau trimārgagām / kālindīṃ chāgameṣāsyau svadakṣāddvāḥsthaśākhayoḥ adhodehalyananteśādhāraśaktīśca pūjayet / dvāramadhye sarasvatyā mahāstraṃ pūjayedamī padmādhāragatāḥ sarve@pyuditā vighnanāśakāḥ / pūjane pūrvavanmantro dīpakadvayakalpitaḥ arghapuṣpasamālambhadhūpanaivedyavandanaiḥ / pūjāṃ kuryādihārghaścāpyuttamadravyayojitaḥ ekoccāreṇa vā kuryāddvāḥsthadaivatapūjanam / rahasyapūjāṃ cetkuryāttadbāhyaparivārakam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v191] One may worship the doorway deities inwardly before the deity according to the visualized sequence. Then, throwing a flower consecrated by the weapon mantra into the blazing shrine, one destroys obstacles.

[tal-a15-v192] Having entered, one should look upon the shrine with a gaze empowered by Śiva's rays; then one should bind the directions with the weapon mantra and cover them all with the armor mantra.

[tal-a15-v193] There the seeker for liberation should enter facing the northern direction, for the fire of Aghora burns away the bonds that bind.

[tal-a15-v194] Even though we speak of directions like east and west, there is no such thing as direction by itself, for no single direction can be cognized without a limiting condition.

[tal-a15-v195] If someone says that direction is just a limiting condition called east and so on, then how could such a mere condition account for real variety?

[tal-a15-v196] Therefore it is this light of consciousness, appearing in the form of objects, that boldly displays the variety known as the division into east and other directions.

[tal-a15-v197] Whatever is always fit to be taken up by light is above, being of the nature of light, while what is unfit for contact is below.

[tal-a15-v198] What is only slightly luminous is the middle, and from that the directions arise; when light spreads toward what can be slightly illuminated, that is the front.

[tal-a15-v199] What is turned away is behind, so front and back arise as a pair; when light faces an object and grasps it, its rays become more abundant.

[tal-a15-v200] Where light stands in conformity, that is called the right; and what stands in front of that right side is taught to be the left.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-dvāḥsthāṃśca pūjayedantardevāgre kalpanākramāt / kṣiptvāstrajaptaṃ kusumaṃ jvaladveśmani vghnanut praviśya śivaraśmīddhadṛśā veśmāvalokayet / diśo@streṇa ca badhnīyācchādayedvarmaṇākhilāḥ tatrottarāśābhimukho mumukṣustādṛśāya vā / viśettathā hyaghorāgniḥ pāśānpluṣyati bandhakān yadyapyasti na diṅnāma kācitpūrvāparādikā / pratyayo hi na tasyāḥ syādekasyā anupāhiteḥ upādhiḥ pūrvatādiṣṭa iti cettatkṛtaṃ diśā / upādhimātraṃ tu tathā vaicitryāya kathaṃ bhavet tasmātsaṃvitprakāśo@yaṃ mūrtyābhāsanabhāgataḥ / pūrvādidigvibhāgākhyavaicitryollekhadurmadaḥ tatra yadyatprakāśena sadā svīkaraṇe kṣamam / tadevordhvaṃ prakāśātma sparśāyogyamadhaḥ punaḥ kiṃcitprakāśatā madhyaṃ tato vai diksamudbhavaḥ / kiṃcitprakāśayogyasya saṃmukhaṃ prasaratpuraḥ parāṅmukhaṃ tu tatpaścāditi digdvayamāgatam / prakāśaḥ saṃmukhaṃ vastu gṛhītvodriktaraśmikaḥ yatra tiṣṭhoddakṣiṇaṃ tatprakāśasyānukūlyataḥ / dakṣiṇasya puraḥsaṃsthaṃ vāmamityupadiśyate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v201] That same illuminated field, gentle like the touch of moonlight, gives rise in this way to the first set of four directions through resting in the middle.

[tal-a15-v202] With another set of four, the directions become eight, each presided over by its own power; all this arises within the supreme, boon-granting light of Śiva.

[tal-a15-v203] The division of directions is established both in the world and in scripture, for Sadāśiva is taught in sequence as having a body made of five mantras.

[tal-a15-v204] By the division into Īśāna, Aghora, Vāma, Sadyojāta, and the lower face, the directions are mapped out: Īśāna is above because of its luminosity, and the extending eastern face corresponds to that light.

[tal-a15-v205] Puruṣa is identified in this scheme, the fierce Aghora is the south, the gentle Vāma is the left, and Sadyojāta, being turned away, is designated as the west.

[tal-a15-v206] The nether face is below because of its lack of luminosity, and indeed space, wind, fire, water, and earth are the faces of that Lord.

[tal-a15-v207] As the primary element, space alone is said to be above and made of light, while below that same principle is clearly non-luminous.

[tal-a15-v208] In the middle, what is luminous is neither merely something to be illuminated nor simply its opposite; because it is seen through luminosity, a set of four directions arises there.

[tal-a15-v209] Thus the Lord whose body is the five mantras is the sovereign of all directions, and after him Īśa, Rudra, Viṣṇu, and Brahmā are likewise established.

[tal-a15-v210] Viṣṇu and Brahmā do not have a fifth face, because they are powers of differentiation concerned with maintenance and creation, not with that higher upward manifestation.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tatprakāśitameyendusparśasaumyaṃ tadeva hi / evamāśācatuṣke@sminmadhyaviśrāntiyogataḥ catuṣkamanyattenāṣṭau diśastattadadhiṣṭhitāḥ / evaṃ prakāśamātre@sminvarade parame śive digvibhāgaḥ sthito loke śāstre@pica tathocyate / kramātsadāśivādhīśaḥ pañcamantratanuryataḥ īśanraghoravāmākhyasadyo@dhobhedato diśaḥ / īśa ūrdhvaṃ prakāśatvātpūrvaṃ vaktraṃ prasāri yat puruṣo dakṣiṇācaṇḍo vāmā vāmastu saumyakaḥ / parāṅmukhatayā sadyaḥ paścimā paribhāṣyate pātālavaktramadharamaprakāśatayā sthiteḥ / khamarudvahnijalabhūkhāni vaktrāṇyamuṣya hi mukhyatvena khamevordhvaṃ prakāśamayamucyate / tadeva mukhyato@dhastādaprakāśaṃ yataḥ sphuṭam madhye tu yatprakāśaṃ tanna prakāśyaṃ na cetarat / prakāśatvāddiśyamānamato@smindikcatuṣṭayam pañcamantratanurnātha itthaṃ viśvadigīśvaraḥ / tato@pīśastathā rudro viṣṇurbrahmā tathā sthitaḥ ūrdhvābhivyaktyayogyatvādviṣṇordhātuśca pañcamam / na vaktraṃ tau bhedamayau sṛṣṭisthitiprabhū yataḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v211] Their division of directions comes from four faces; if a fifth were joined to them, those two would abandon their own nature.

[tal-a15-v212] Therefore, even within the cosmic egg, the Lord's power of knowledge, appearing as the sun dense with light, makes the division of the directions.

[tal-a15-v213] For example, at the equinox, where the sun is first seen is called east, and where its shadow falls is called west.

[tal-a15-v214] As the sun moves on its course, what lies to its left is the south, where it shines with fierce rays as if blazing intensely.

[tal-a15-v215] What lies in front of that is the left, slightly touched by its light; therefore it is gentle, yet not without light.

[tal-a15-v216] Where the sun sets is established as the west; and even there, for some, the earlier light can still be seen.

[tal-a15-v217] That same order was determined before for these as in sound; that direction is so, and its fruit-giving remains even in reversal.

[tal-a15-v218] Varied fruit-attainment depends on light; thus direction may be sun-dependent, various, and such.

[tal-a15-v219] Presided over by the great lord bearing varied form; what more need be said of the worshipper facing that?

[tal-a15-v220] Directions are divided east, south, north, west; that direction-division made according to own course is always Shiva.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-digvibhāgastu tajjo@sti vadanānāṃ catuṣṭayāt / pañcamasya yujitve tau parityaktanijātmakau tato brahmāṇḍamadhye@pi jñānaśaktirvibho raviḥ / diśāṃ vibhāgaṃ kurute prakāśaghanavṛttimān tathāhi viṣuvadyoge yataḥ pūrvaṃ pradṛśyate / tatpūrva yatra tacchāyā tatpaścimamudāhṛtam tasmiñjigamiṣorasya yatsavyaṃ tattu dakṣiṇam / tatraiṣa caṇḍatejobhirbhāti jājvalyamānavat tatpurovarti vāmaṃ tu tadbhāsā khacitaṃ manāk / tata eva hi somyaṃ tannacāpi hyaprakāśakam yatrāsāvastamabhyeti tatpaścimamiti sthitiḥ / tatraiva paścime yeṣāṃ prākprakāśāvalokanam tadeva pūrvameteṣāṃ yathādhvani nirūpitam / sā sā dikca tathā tasya phaladāpi viparyaye vicitre phalasaṃpattiḥ prakāśādhīnikā yataḥ / itthaṃ sūryāśrayā diksyātsā vicitrāpi tādṛśī adhiṣṭhitā maheśena citratadrūpadhāriṇā / kiṃ vātibahunā yo@sau yaṣṭā tatsaṃmukhāditaḥ diśo@pi pravibhajyante prāksavyottarapaścimāḥ / svānusārakṛtaṃ taṃ ca digvibhāgaṃ sadā śivaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v221] He presides like the sun from varied body; even self-risen directions have own lords, and Indra and others indeed preside.

[tal-a15-v222] They are indeed portions of light-power, following light; whatever lordship of light is Indra, but that greatness is something else.

[tal-a15-v223] He is fire in the controller-desired state; Yama, Raksha, then those; Varuna and that; from unsteadiness air is called.

[tal-a15-v224] By accumulation of being, the wealth-lord at its decay is all-pervading; unseen form, endless; above Brahma, expander, all-pervading.

[tal-a15-v225] Power-portions of light only; world-guardians are declared by that. Thus even self-dependent form; direction-sun is taught.

[tal-a15-v226] There all indeed attains unwavering light-nature, as all-pervading wind is fanned by a fan.

[tal-a15-v227] The awakened would do his own action, duty-removal and so on; like that, all-pervading, all Indra-powers clearly.

[tal-a15-v228] Adepts awakened by breath give various desired fruit; thus sun-power with direction-lords, Brahma, Vishnu, Isha, Sau, Shiva.

[tal-a15-v229] Presided over by firm reassurance, giving various fruit; the adept may worship field, mandala, or house.

[tal-a15-v230] Standing according to that, Shankara becomes middle; he indeed is all-presider by middleness, its who.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-adhitiṣṭhatyarkamiva sa vicitravapuryataḥ / svotthā api diśaḥ sveśāḥ śakrādyā hyadhiśerate te hi prakāśaśaktyaṃśāḥ prakāśānuvidhāyinaḥ / prakāśasya yadaiśvaryaṃ sa indro yattu tanmahaḥ so@gniryantṛtvabhīmatve yamo rakṣastadūnimā / prakāśyaṃ varuṇastacca cāñcalyādvāyurucyate bhāvasañcayayogena vitteśastatkṣaye vibhuḥ / adṛṣṭavigraho@nanto brahmordhve vṛṃhako vibhuḥ prakāśasyaiva śaktyaṃśā lokapāstena kīrtitāḥ / itthaṃ svādhīnarūpāpi diksaurī tūpadiśyate tatra sarvo hi niṣkampaṃ prakāśatvaṃ prapadyate / sarvago@pyanilo yadvadvyajanenopavījitaḥ prabuddhaḥ svāṃ kriyāṃ kuryāddharmanirṇodanādikām / tadvatsarvagatāḥ sarvā aindyādyāḥ śaktayaḥ sphuṭam sādhakāśvāsasaṃbuddhāstattatsveṣṭaphalapradāḥ / evaṃ saurī digīśānabrahmaviṣṇvīśasauśivaiḥ adhiṣṭhitā samāśvāsadārḍhyāttattatphalapradā / sādhako yacca vā kṣetraṃ maṇḍalaṃ veśma vā bhajet sthitastadanusāreṇa madhyībhavati śaṃkaraḥ / sa hi sarvamadhiṣṭhātā mādhyasthyeneti tasya yaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v231] Sun-related light before thus may be direction-establishment; of the lord standing in the middle, to grasp southern greatness.

[tal-a15-v232] North-facing may be to grasp western; east-facing, having sat in own place, should perform body-purification.

[tal-a15-v233] Weapon risen as flame from thumb tip; having meditated, by its flames burn the body outside and inside.

[tal-a15-v234] Burning and destruction are thus called; destroyer named mantra; radiance thus named own thought-essence.

[tal-a15-v235] By that mantra-fire burning in body and eightfold city, so from destruction of body-city-ego arises.

[tal-a15-v236] Not indeed by mere existence is the body like another body; in egoity indeed is bodiness; that destroyed, that burns certainly.

[tal-a15-v237] Burden of body-purification as ash then who standing; shaking him with armor-wind, should stand in pure consciousness-self.

[tal-a15-v238] In that steady waveless, having attained absorption, of consciousness, from creative nature first attains waviness.

[tal-a15-v239] That itself form thus called, syllable-bindu-essence; then by nine-soul-god placement principle-rising-essence.

[tal-a15-v240] Limbs and faces of that itself in own places should be placed; then by matrika as before various principle clarity essence.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sauraḥ prakāśastatpūrvamitthaṃ syāddigvyavasthitiḥ / tanmadhyasthitanāthasya grahītuṃ dakṣiṇaṃ mahaḥ udaṅmukhaḥ syāt pāścātyaṃ grahītuṃ pūrvatomukhaḥ / upaviśya nijasthāne dehaśuddhiṃ samācaret aṅguṣṭhāgrātkālavahnijvālābhāsvaramutthitam / astraṃ dhyātvā tacchikhābhirbahirantardahettanum dāhaśca dhvaṃsa evokto dhvaṃsakaṃ mantrasaṃjñitam / tejastathābhilāpākhyasvavikalparasombhitam tena mantrāgninā dāho dehe puryaṣṭake tathā / dehapuryaṣṭakāhantāvidhvaṃsādeva jāyate nahi sadbhāvamātreṇa deho@sāvanyadehavat / ahantāyāṃ hi dehatvaṃ sā dhvastā taddaheddhruvam taddehasaṃskārabharo bhasmatvenātha yaḥ sthitaḥ / taṃ varmavāyunādhūya tiṣṭhecchuddhacidātmani tasmindhruve nistaraṅge samāpattimupāgataḥ / saṃvidaḥ sṛṣṭidharmitvādādyāmeti taraṅgitām saiva mūrtiriti khyātā tārasadbinduhātmikā / tato navātmadevena nyāsastattvodayātmakaḥ aṅgavaktrāṇi tasyaiva svasthāneṣu niyojayet / atha mātṛkayā prāgvattattattvasphuṭatātmakaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v241] On the back, extending through the three regions, one performs the installation of the three principles. Then comes the installation of the eight Ghoras, with the head formed by their feet.

[tal-a15-v242] Then comes the installation of the being of Shiva, joined with one's own body. When this fivefold set has been performed, whatever holds primacy within it should become the main focus.

[tal-a15-v243] In the sixth installation, one should place the object of contemplation and worship together with its limbs. Therefore, the Lord Ratiśekhara is the one fit to be installed here.

[tal-a15-v244] The ninefold is to be installed above. When it is given primacy, the other is placed in a different abode. The same rule applies if the being of Bhairava is made primary.

[tal-a15-v245] Ratiśekhara is to be installed beforehand in the place appropriate to what is being worshipped. This is how the tradition was set forth to me in the Śrīpūrva scripture.

[tal-a15-v246] In the procedure of installation, the Lord Śambhu is the deity. How could he be excluded? His limbs also exist and are part of it.

[tal-a15-v247] The form, emanation, and the three principles, together with the form and limbs, are to be understood as belonging to Shiva with his limbs. The installation is declared to be sixfold.

[tal-a15-v248] Above this, one should then perform the sixfold Shakta installation. First comes Parāparā with her faces, and thus Mālinī at the beginning.

[tal-a15-v249] After that, the triad beginning with Parā is installed in order at the crest, heart, and feet. Then the sequence continues through the head, face, throat, heart, navel, secret place, and thighs.

[tal-a15-v250] The sequence beginning with Aghorā is placed in the knee and foot. Then come the five limbs of the vidyā. After that, one should invoke the Shakti whose form is the being of the Mother.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tritattvanyāsatā cāsya pṛṣṭhe kakṣyātrayāgate / tato@ghorāṣṭakanyāsaḥ śirastaccaraṇātmakam tato@pi śivasadbhāvanyāsaḥ svāṃgasya saṃyutaḥ / ittha kṛte pañcake@sminyattanmukhyatayā bhavet upāsyamarcyaṃ tatsāṅgaṃ ṣaṣṭhe nyāse niyojayet / tenātra nyāsayogyo@sau bhagavānratiśekharaḥ ūrdhve nyāsyo navākhyasya mukhyatve@nyonyadhāmatā / evaṃ bhairavasadbhāvanāthe mukhyatayā yadi upāsyatā tattatsthāna prāṅnyāsyo ratiśekharaḥ / itthaṃ śrīpūrvaśāstre me saṃpradāyaṃ nyarūpayat śaṃbhunātho nyāsavidhau devo hi kathamanyathā / nyāsa vivarjyate@muṣminnaṅgānyapyasya santi hi mūrtiḥ sṛṣṭistritattvaṃ cetyaṣṭau mūrtyaṅgasaṃyutāḥ / śivaḥ sāṅgaśca vijñeyo nyāsaḥ ṣoḍhā prakīrtitaḥ asyopari tataḥ śāktaṃ nyāsaṃ kuryācca ṣaḍvidham / parāparāṃ savaktrāṃ prāktataḥ prāgiti mālinīm paścātparāditritayaṃ śikhāhṛtpādagaṃ kramāt / tataḥ kavaktrakaṇṭheṣu hṛnnābhīguhya+ūrutaḥ jānupāde@pyaghoryādyaṃ tato vidyāṅgapañcakam / tatastvāvāhayecchaktiṃ mātṛsadbhāvarūpiṇīm

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v251] One invokes Yogeśvarī, the supreme, full, steadfast Kālasaṃkarṣiṇī, augmented by the twelve Shaktis of her limbs, faces, and retinue.

[tal-a15-v252] At the time of installation, the guru should contemplate according to the aim and practice of the rite. The supreme goddess, abiding in the middle of the triad, is the non-differentiating one.

[tal-a15-v253] She is proclaimed as the being of unlimited consciousness alone. This is declared in the Sāra scripture and in the Yāmala, and therefore this is how the goddess is understood.

[tal-a15-v254] The form with faces, the Shakti, the triad of Shaktis, the group of eight, the five limbs, and the supreme Shakti make up the Shakta installation, which is also sixfold.

[tal-a15-v255] This Yāmala great installation gives the fruits of accomplishment and liberation. But one who seeks liberation alone should first perform the Shakta installation.

[tal-a15-v256] The gurus say that for one who desires liberation, the pair of installations described should be performed beginning with the feet, in the order of withdrawal.

[tal-a15-v257] However many divisions are declared as denoting Śambhu, Shakti, and the individual, in all those mantras the installation is proclaimed as sixfold.

[tal-a15-v258] But the mantra that is invoked, endowed with its limbs, should be the sixth. Thus in all cases this installation is stated as sixfold.

[tal-a15-v259] Afterward come the display of mudrās by body, mind, and speech. There are the five states beginning with waking, and a sixth called the unsurpassed.

[tal-a15-v260] Because of the six causes, the sixfold selfhood, and the joining of the thirty-six principles, when the sixfold great installation is performed, this whole universe is powerfully brought into unity.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-yogeśvarīṃ parāṃ pūrṇāṃ kālasaṃkarṣiṇīṃ dhruvām / aṅgavaktraparīvāraśaktidvādaśakādhikām sādhyānuṣṭhānabhedena nyāsakāle smaredguruḥ / paraiva devītritayamadhye yābhedinī sthitā sānavacchedacinmātrasadbhāveyaṃ prakīrtitā / sāraśāstre yāmale ca devyāstena prakīrtitaḥ mūrtiḥ savaktrā śaktiśca śaktitrayamathāṣṭakam / pañcāṅgāni parā śaktirnyāsaḥ śākto@pi ṣaḍvidhaḥ yāmalo@yaṃ mahānyāsaḥ siddhimuktiphalapradaḥ / muktyekārthī punaḥ pūrvaṃ śāktaṃ nyāsaṃ samācaret guravastvāhuritthaṃ yannyāsadvayamudāhṛtam / mumukṣuṇā tu pādādi tatkāryaṃ saṃhṛtikramāt yāvantaḥ kīrtitā bhedāḥ śaṃbhuśaktyaṇuvācakāḥ / tāvatsvapyeṣu mantreṣu nyāsaḥ ṣoḍhaiva kīrtitaḥ kiṃtvāvāhyastu yo mantraḥ sa tatrāṅgasamanvitaḥ / ṣaṣṭhaḥ syāditi sarvatra ṣoḍhaivāyamudāhṛtaḥ mudrāpradarśanaṃ paścātkāyena manasā girā / pañcāvasthā jāgradādyāḥ ṣaṣṭhyanuttaranāmikā ṣaṭkāraṇaṣaḍātmatvātṣaṭtriṃśattattvayojanam / evaṃ ṣoḍhāmahānyāse kṛte viśvamidaṃ haṭhāt

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v261] Having attained identity in the body, one should reveal a pure emanation. Beginning from the installation of the form, the emanation that has spread forth here is that pure emanation.

[tal-a15-v262] By the power and order of the installation, the emanation is brought to non-difference and made pure. Therefore those deluded people who object regarding the shaking off of the burning of bonds are mistaken.

[tal-a15-v263] When one is established in peaceful Shiva, why would he descend again? Those who ask this are refuted from the outset, for they do not understand the ultimate reality of Śambhu.

[tal-a15-v264] They do not know, because they are devoid of the essence of the flashing of their own awareness. For this peaceful Shiva is not some differentiated entity.

[tal-a15-v265] Anything excluded from all other paths is limited somewhere, like a pot. But this consciousness, whose nature is great light, truly expands.

[tal-a15-v266] That consciousness is Shiva, and Shiva's nature is to appear as all forms. Therefore, through that very manifestation, he expands by his own essence.

[tal-a15-v267] In this manifestation, both non-difference and difference of one's own self appear. When difference expands, maya unfolds, and with it the maya-bound subject comes into play.

[tal-a15-v268] When non-difference expands, that very maya-bound subject unfolds into Shiva-nature. The maya-bound subject attains this through skill gained by practicing identification with that form.

[tal-a15-v269] Shiva alone is declared to be the fruit of that practice, including nyasa and the rest. For just as one becomes shaped by contemplating, 'I am a doer of bad deeds,' so too contemplation determines one's state.

[tal-a15-v270] So too, for one who contemplates, 'I am Shiva, I am no other,' the result follows accordingly. This alone is called firmness: when it has gone to the very heart of reflective awareness.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-dehe tādātmyamāpannaṃ śuddhāṃ sṛṣṭiṃ prakāśayet / mūrtinyāsātsamārabhya yā sṛṣṭiḥ prasṛtātra sā abhedamānīya kṛtā śuddhā nyāsabalakramāt / tena ye@codayanmūḍhāḥ pāśadāhavidhūnane kṛte śānte śive rūḍhaḥ punaḥ kimavarohati / iti te dūrato dhvastāḥ paramārthaṃ hi śāṃbhavam na vidusta svasaṃvittisphurattāsāravarjitāḥ / na khalveṣa śivaḥ śānto nāma kaścidvibhedavān sarvetarādhvavyāvṛtto ghaṭatulyo@sti kutracit / mahāprakāśarūpā hi yeyaṃ saṃvidvijṛmbhate sa śivaḥ śivataivāsya vaiśvarūpyāvabhāsitā / tathābhāsanayogo@taḥ svarasenāsya jṛmbhate bhāsyamāno@tra cābhedaḥ svātmano bheda eva ca / bhede vijṛmbhite māyā māyāmāturvijṛmbhate abhede jṛmbhate@syaiva māyāmātuḥ śivātmatā / māyāpramātā tadrūpavikalpābhyāsapāṭavāt śiva eva tadabhyāsaphalaṃ nyāsādi kīrtitam / yathāhi duṣṭakarmāsmītyevaṃ bhāvayatastathā tathā śivo@haṃ nānyo@smītyevaṃ bhāvayatastathā / etadevocyate dārḍhyaṃ vimarśahṛdayaṅgamam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v271] The non-conceptual state is reached through streams of thought centered on identity with Shiva. Otherwise, how could that pure reality, which lives by the very life of reflective awareness, be approached?

[tal-a15-v272] How could any form of that whose nature is to shine ever remain unexamined by awareness? Therefore, by the power of its sovereign free will, this reality accomplishes even what seems most difficult.

[tal-a15-v273] Even though breath, intellect, and the like appear to shine, one should not conceive them as having their own independent nature. On the contrary, their nature is opposite to that of the supremely free self.

[tal-a15-v274] If one ascertains these faculties only as perishable and dependent on the Lord, one sinks into a certainty that cuts one off into participation in samsara.

[tal-a15-v275] Instead, one should take refuge in a non-conceptual abiding that comes through certainty in the eternal and so forth. But those who are endowed with purity born of the most intense descent of grace are different.

[tal-a15-v276] It has been explained that those purified by the most intense grace do not perform initiation and nyasa. But in this way, one who has the universe as his body clearly attains the state of being the universal self.

[tal-a15-v277] From nyasa alone, the body becomes transformed in that way, and one should worship it with flowers and other offerings. This may be done in detail with separate mantras, or briefly with the root mantra.

[tal-a15-v278] With incense, food offerings, acts of satisfaction, and so on, worship may be done in elaborate or concise form. Because samsara moves in a leftward way, all of this should be done with the left hand.

[tal-a15-v279] The teacher should also perform the rite of offering with that unimpaired hand. In the revered Matanga and other texts, the word 'left' is said to signify the secret.

[tal-a15-v280] The mantra practitioner devoted to left practice should perform the worship; this is stated clearly in the revered Bharga-shikha scripture and likewise in the revered Agama teaching.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-śivaikātmyavikalpaughadvārikā nirvikalpatā / anyathā tasya śuddhasya vimarśaprāṇavartinaḥ kathaṃ nāmāvimṛṣṭaṃ syādrūpaṃ bhāsanadharmaṇaḥ / tenātidurghaṭaghaṭāsvatantrecchāvaśādayam bhānapi prāṇabuddhyādiḥ svaṃ tathā na vikalpayet / pratyutātisvatantrātmaviparītasvadharmatām vināśyanīśāyattatvarūpāṃ niścitya majjati / tataḥ saṃsārabhāgīyatathāniścayaśātinīm nityādiniścayadvārāmavikalpāṃ sthitiṃ śrayet / ye tu tīvratamodriktaśaktinirmalatājuṣaḥ na te dīkṣāmanunyāsakāriṇaśceti varṇitam / evaṃ viśvaśarīraḥ sanviśvātmatvaṃ gataḥ sphuṭam nyāsamātrāt tathābhūtaṃ dehaṃ puṣpādinārcayet / pṛthaṅmantrairvistareṇa saṃkṣepānmūlamantrataḥ dhūpanaivedyatṛptyādyaistathā vyāsasamāsataḥ / saṃsāravāmācāratvātsarvaṃ vāmakareṇa tu kuryāttarpaṇayogaṃ ca daiśikastadanāmayā / vāmaśabdena guhyaṃ śrīmataṅgādāvapīritam vāmācāraparo mantrī yāgaṃ kuryāditi sphuṭam / śrīmadbhargaśikhāśāstre tathā śrīgamaśāsane

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v281] Whatever merit there is in all sacred places and whatever fruit there is in all sacrifices, that fruit, O beloved, is multiplied ten million times by offering to the unimpaired one.

[tal-a15-v282] In the revered Nandi-shikha and in the revered Ananda teaching it is said that the ladle should be full, and the spoon should be used in the offering of ghee.

[tal-a15-v283] The rest, including worship, fire offering, recitation, and so on, should be done with the left hand alone. In this way the body becomes filled with bliss and free from turning outward toward everything.

[tal-a15-v284] Having accomplished the body through worship, one should contemplate it as of Shiva-nature. When outward turning toward objects has dissolved and limitation has melted away, this contemplation becomes clear.

[tal-a15-v285] When limitation has dissolved, what would remain in the body apart from the essence of Shiva-bliss? The body is filled with the essence of Shiva-bliss and pervaded by the thirty-six principles.

[tal-a15-v286] Seeing and worshipping the body day and night, one becomes of Shiva-nature. Such a person is satisfied, resting in the body as the universal self and established in its sign.

[tal-a15-v287] Such a person does not desire external observances like linga vows, sacred places, and similar practices. The rites were taught so that consciousness might come to rest, and for one in whom it already rests, that is enough.

[tal-a15-v288] The higher rites, extending up to external worship, are to be accomplished here for the sake of realizing Shiva-nature. Therefore, the offering vessel should be made as the supreme reality consisting of non-difference from Shiva.

[tal-a15-v289] Just as in the body there is a progression from burning to worship, so too the act is full of bliss-essence and satisfies all world-deities.

[tal-a15-v290] Even in the argha vessel, by summary and expansion, which substances are for sacrifice and what argha is, is not declared.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sarvatīrtheṣu yatpuṇyaṃ sarvayajñeṣu yatphalam / tatphalaṃ koṭiguṇitamanāmātarpaṇātpriye śrīmannandiśikhāyāṃ ca śrīmadānandaśāsane / taduktaṃ srukca pūrṇāyāṃ sruvaśvājyāhutau bhavet śeṣaṃ vāmakareṇaiva pūjāhomajapādikam / evamānandasaṃpūrṇaṃ sarvaunmukhyavivarjitam yāgena dehaṃ miṣpādya bhāvayeta śivātmakam / galite viṣayaunmukhye pārimitye vilāpite dehe kimavaśiṣyeta śivānandarasādṛte / śivānandarasāpūrṇaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśattattvanirbharam dehaṃ divāniśaṃ paśyannarcayansyācchivātmakaḥ / viśvātmadehaviśrāntitṛptastalliṅganiṣṭhitaḥ bāhyaṃ liṅgavratakṣetracaryādi nahi vāñchati / tāvanmātrāttvaviśrānteḥ saṃvidaḥ kathitāḥ kriyāḥ uttarā bāhyayāgāntāḥ sādhyā tvatra śivātmatā / tato@rghapātraṃ kartavyaṃ śivābhedamayaṃ param ānandarasasaṃpūrṇaṃ viśvadaivatatarpaṇam / yathaiva dehe dāhādipūjāntaṃ tadvadeva hi arghapātre@pi kartavyaṃ samāsavyāsayogataḥ / kāni dravyāṇi yāgāya ko nvargha iti noditam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v291] For one desiring siddhi, the means is indeed the cause in that siddhi; for one desiring liberation, nothing is forbidden and nothing is prescribed.

[tal-a15-v292] Whatever is pleasing is suitable in Shiva-consciousness distinction; having made the argha vessel, sprinkle it with drops and offer flowers and such.

[tal-a15-v293] Having made by that, one should worship oneself as supreme Shiva, from fear of confusion of flowers given in argha worship.

[tal-a15-v294] Do not put a flower in the argha vessel for deity worship; in the argha vessel it becomes nectar-water, and that is worshipped.

[tal-a15-v295] For satisfaction of mantras and purification of sacrifice substances only; thus, having worshipped the body, one addresses forms empty of prana and intellect.

[tal-a15-v296] Worship those who have become mutually identified, in such a Shiva state, when nyasa of prana-support is fashioned by intellect.

[tal-a15-v297] From the empty base all is worshipped by one effort; but place the support-power four fingers below the navel.

[tal-a15-v298] Earth, the ocean of gods, and fire; vessel-form and wind-stalk nature, from the world-thread installation.

[tal-a15-v299] Place four at each finger, sky-womb, slightly all around, pure, essence-like.

[tal-a15-v300] Then make the staff named Ananta up to the uvula, ending in tanmatras and kalas; above that is a knot of night-nature.
