chunks.sanskrit: [and]-siddhikāmasya tatsiddhau sādhanaiva hi kāraṇam / muktikāmasya no kiṃcinniṣiddhaṃ vihitaṃ ca no yadeva hṛdyaṃ tadyogyaṃ śivasaṃvidabhedane / kṛtvārghapātraṃ tadvipruṭprokṣitaṃ kusumādikam kṛtvā ca tena svātmānaṃ pūjayetparamaṃ śivam / arghapātrārcanādattapuṣpasaṃkīrṇatābhayāt nārghapātre@tra kusumaṃ kuryāddevārcanākṛte / arghapātre tadamṛtībhūtamambveva pūjitam mantrāṇāṃ tṛptaye yāgadravyaśuddhyai ca kevalam / evaṃ dehaṃ pūjayitvā prāṇadhīśūnyavigrahān anyonyatanmayībhūtān pūjayecchivatādṛśe / tatra prāṇāśraye nayāse buddhyā viracite sati śūnyādhiṣṭhānataḥ sarvamekayatnena pūjyate / nyasyedādhāraśaktiṃ tu nābhyadhaścaturaṅgulām dharāṃ surodaṃ tejaśca meyapārapratiṣṭhiteḥ / potarūpaṃ marutkandasvabhāvaṃ viśvasūtraṇāt pratyekamaṅgulaṃ nyasyeccatuṣkaṃ vyomagarbhakam / īṣatsamantādamalamidamāmalasārakam tato daṇḍamanantākhyaṃ kalpayellambikāvadhi / tanmātrādikalāntaṃ tadūrdhve granthirniśātmakaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v301] In that maya-made knot are eight beginning with dharma and adharma; fire and such are maya; its offspring is vibhava, and intellect.

[tal-a15-v302] Above the maya knot, meditate the four below the trident, of pure-vidya nature, joined with two coverings.

[tal-a15-v303] That tattva is situated and to be meditated between uvula and brahmarandhra; light-yoga occurs there, with sight, hearing, taste, and such.

[tal-a15-v304] Place eighteen shaktis clockwise from the right in the vidya lotus here; that was also said before and is shown again.

[tal-a15-v305] Vama, Jyeshtha, Raudri, Kali, Kalabalavikarika, Balamathani, Bhutadamani, and Manonmanika, Shanta; Shakracaparucira may be here.

[tal-a15-v306] Vibhvi, Jnaptikriti, Iccha, Vagishi, Jvalini, and Vama, Jyeshtha, Raudri—these from the eastern petal, all like time-burning.

[tal-a15-v307] In the petal-filament centers, remember the sun-moon-fire triad, presided by its own lords Brahma, Vishnu, and Hara.

[tal-a15-v308] The form beyond maya of Brahma and others was previously stated; this seat is indeed that, not smeared with maya collyrium.

[tal-a15-v309] Above Rudra place Ishvara god, and above that Sadasiva; he is called Mahapreta in the scriptures.

[tal-a15-v310] Mahapreta, by pervading all tattvas, is absorbed from awakening and excellent going, and would not go downward.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tatra māyāmaye granthau dharmādharmādyamaṣṭakam / vahniprāgādi māyā hi tatsūtirvibhavastu dhīḥ māyāgrantherūrdhvabhūmau triśūlādhaścatuṣkikām / śuddhavidyātmikāṃ dhyāyecchadanadvayasaṃyutām tacca tattvaṃ sthitaṃ bhāvyaṃ lambikābrahmarandhrayoḥ / prakāśayogo hyatraivaṃ dṛkśrotrarasanādikaḥ dakṣānyāvartato nyasyecchaktīnāṃ navakadvayam / vidyāpadme@tra taccoktamapi prāgdarśyate punaḥ vāmā jyeṣṭhā raudrī kālī kalabalavikarike balamathanī / bhūtadamanī ca manonmanikā śāntā śakracāparuciratra syāt vibhvī jñaptikṛtīcchā vāgīśī jvālinī tathā vāmā / jyeṣṭhā raudrītyetāḥ prāgdalataḥ kāladahanavatsarvāḥ dalakesaramadhyeṣu sūryendudahanatrayam / nijādhipairbrahmaviṣṇuharaiścādhiṣṭhitaṃ smaret māyottīrṇaṃ hi yadrūpaṃ brahmādīnāṃ puroditam / āsanaṃ tvetadeva syānnatu māyāñjanāñjitam rudrordhve ceśvaraṃ devaṃ tadūrdhve ca sadāśivam / nyasyetsa ca mahāpreta iti śāstreṣu bhaṇyate samastatattvavyāptṛtvānmahāpretaḥ prabodhataḥ / prakarṣagamanāccaiṣa līno yannādharaṃ vrajet

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v311] All lords of vidya and avidya, having gone higher and higher and become Sadasiva, then resort to supreme Shiva.

[tal-a15-v312] Therefore Sadasiva is always upward-gazing luminous self; he is thin due to measurability and weakness, a preta from loud laughter and such.

[tal-a15-v313] Remember the sound-end self, pervaded by Śakti and bright in mind, risen from the navel and exited through the three crown openings.

[tal-a15-v314] Three spokes, twelve-ended, there also beyond-mind three; of white lotuses, this is the thirty-seven-self seat.

[tal-a15-v315] Here all principles with distinction-breath; from that, distinct as seat, indeed the object of consciousness is remembered.

[tal-a15-v316] These very principles are dissolved in supreme Bhairava; then by identity they are created in distinction-deva-worship-joining.

[tal-a15-v317] Having Śrī Bhairava knowledge-unity gain freedom, these very principles attain worshipper-hood enough.

[tal-a15-v318] The worshipper is supreme-principle self; the worshipped principle is supreme-inferior, and because created, the inferior principle-net is the seat-state foundation.

[tal-a15-v319] In Siddhānta it ends at vidyā-kalā; in left-right scriptures at Sadāśiva; in Mata Yāmala at Samanā.

[tal-a15-v320] Ending at unmanā, here called this supreme seat; having worshipped the seat, the worshipped guru line is as Bhāvin.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-vidyāvidyeśinaḥ sarve hyuttarottaratāṃ gatāḥ / sadāśivībhūya tataḥ paraṃ śivamupāśritāḥ ataḥ sadāśivo nityamūrdhvadṛgbhāsvarātmakaḥ / kṛśo meyatvadaurbalyātpreto@ṭṭahasanāditaḥ tasya nābhyutthitaṃ mūrdharandhratrayavinirgatam / nādāntātma smarecchaktivyāpinīsamanojjvalam arātrayaṃ dviṣaṭkāntaṃ tatrāpyaunmanasaṃ trayam / paṅkajānāṃ sitaṃ saptatriṃśadātmedamāsanam atra sarvāṇi tattvāni bhedaprāṇāni yattataḥ / āsanatvena bhinnaṃ hi saṃvido viṣayaḥ smṛtaḥ etānyeva tu tattvāni līnāni parabhairave / tādātmyenātha sṛṣṭāni bhidevārcyatvayojane śrīmadbhairavabodhaikyalābhasvātantryavanti tu / etānyeva tu tattvāni pūjakatvaṃ prayāntyalam pūjakaḥ paratattvātmā pūjyaṃ tattvaṃ parāparam / sṛṣṭatvādaparaṃ tattvajālamāsanatāspadam vidyākalāntaṃ siddhānte vāmadakṣiṇaśāstrayoḥ / sadāśivāntaṃ samanāparyantaṃ matayāmale unmanāntamihākhyātamityetatparamāsanam / arcayitvāsanaṃ pūjyā gurupaṅktistu bhāvivat

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v321] In that seat, formerly embodied, with half-syllable, two; place as pervader-ness, thus said in Siddha Yogīśvarī Mata.

[tal-a15-v322] Worship Sadāśiva, great preta image, with half-syllable, as supreme above, with incense, flowers, etc., thus.

[tal-a15-v323] Imagine the vidyā-image, then self-named, second; in the middle Bhairava true-being, on the right Rati-crest.

[tal-a15-v324] Nine-self; on the left that devī-like Bhairava triad; in the middle supreme full-moon image; on the right again.

[tal-a15-v325] The higher-lower form is red and slightly pointed, not terrifying; the lower form on the left horn is terrifying and black-tawny.

[tal-a15-v326] After placement is done in the body as before, twofold and sixfold, one should then imagine the fitting imagined form of these.

[tal-a15-v327] According to action difference, forms with two, four, or six arms and so on bear skull, trident, club, boon, fear, pot, and so on.

[tal-a15-v328] One imagines because of variegated left-right placement, since in reality these goddesses are universal forms of consciousness-nature.

[tal-a15-v329] Their essence is unlimited consciousness alone, for liberation; then all limbs, faces, and so on, world-guardians, weapons, last.

[tal-a15-v330] In the middle the goddess-named worshipful triad becomes and is worshiped, then from the middle-seated mass of consciousness and eternal unity.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tatrāsane purā mūrtibhūtāṃ sārdhākṣarāṃ dvayīm / nyasyedvyāptṛtayetyuktaṃ siddhayogīśvarīmate sadāśivaṃ mahāpretaṃ mūrtiṃ sārdhākṣarāṃ yajet / paratvena parāmūrdhve gandhapuṣpādibhistviti vidyāmūrtimathātmākhyāṃ dvitīyāṃ parikalpayet / madhye bhairavasadbhāvaṃ dakṣiṇe ratiśekharam navātmānaṃ vāmatastaddevīvadbhairavatrayam / madhye parāṃ pūrṇacandrapratimāṃ dakṣiṇe punaḥ parāparāṃ raktavarṇāṃ kiṃcidagrāṃ na bhīṣaṇām / aparāṃ vāmaśṛṅge tu bhīṣaṇāṃ kṛṣṇapiṅgalām prāgvaddvidhātra ṣoḍhaiva nyāso dehe yathā kṛtaḥ / tataḥ sāṃkalpikaṃ yuktaṃ vapurāsāṃ vicintayet kṛtyabhedānusāreṇa dvicatuḥṣaḍbhujādikam / kapālaśūlakhaṭvāṅgavarābhayaghaṭādikam vāmadakṣiṇasaṃsthānacitratvātparikalpayet / vastuto viśvarūpāstā devyo bodhātmikā yataḥ anavacchinnacinmātrasārāḥ syurapavṛktaye / sarvaṃ tato@ṅgavaktrādi lokapālāstrapaścimam madhye devyabhidhā pūjyā trayaṃ bhavati pūjitam / tato madhyagatāttasmādbodharāśeḥ sadaivatāt

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v331] The emanated limbs and so on are worshipful and spark-natured, separate; the goddess going in the middle is indeed she, formed of true being.

[tal-a15-v332] The time-drawing goddess is fierce, peaceful, and mixed everywhere; in the siddha tantra the supreme goddess with one syllable is thus praised.

[tal-a15-v333] The supreme mother goddess Mālinī, middle-risen, is in the middle; one should place there the all-letters-composed supreme sun-radiance.

[tal-a15-v334] At her crest-tip is indeed the one-syllabled; her limbs and so on are thus; then the universe emerged and is worshiped in south and north.

[tal-a15-v335] It may indeed be worshiped by that; once in the middle one should worship, as said in the Shridevi tantra sacrifice named Damara.

[tal-a15-v336] At the nose-tip is threefold time; the time-drawing goddess, always situated in the mouth and calculating breath and inbreath, draws in the heart.

[tal-a15-v337] Through inhalations and retentions it holds and seizes time, but through exhalation it completely seizes all time; rising with the exhalation, it does so in an instant.

[tal-a15-v338] The supreme will-power, by name the awakener of the three powers, is to be worshipped; it draws in all and shatters the very support of time.

[tal-a15-v339] O Shiva, the powers of seeing, action, and will, when engaged in the gross and subtle cutting of the knowable, become in order the sakala and the pralayākala.

[tal-a15-v340] When pure but asleep, the powers become the knowledge-limited state; when awakened, knowing some divided knowables, they are called mantras.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-aṅgādi niḥsṛtaṃ pūjyaṃ visphuliṅgātmakaṃ pṛthak / madhyagā kila yā devī saiva sadbhāvarūpiṇī kālasaṃkarṣiṇī ghorā śāntā miśrā ca sarvataḥ / siddhātantre ca saikārṇā parā devīti kīrtitā parā tu mātṛkā devī mālinī madhyagoditā / madhye nyasyetsūryaruciṃ sarvākṣaramayīṃ parām tasyāḥ śikhāgre tvaikārṇāṃ tasyāścāṅgādikaṃ tviti / tato viśvaṃ viniṣkrāntaṃ pūjitaṃ dakṣiṇottare syādeva pūjitaṃ tena sakṛnmadhye prapūjayet / śrīdevyāyāmale coktaṃ yāge ḍāmarasaṃjñite nāsāgre trividhaṃ kālaṃ kālasaṃkarṣiṇī sadā / mukhasthā śvāsaniḥśvāsakalanī hṛdi karṣati pūrakaiḥ kumbhakairdhatte grasate recakena tu / kālaṃ saṃgrasate sarvaṃ recakenotthitā kṣaṇāt icchāśaktiḥ parā nāmnā śaktitritayabodhinī / yājyā karṣati yatsarvaṃ kālādhāraprabhañjanam iha kila dṛkkarmecchāḥ śiva uktāstāstu vedyakhaṇḍanake / sthūle sūkṣme kramaśaḥ sakalapralayākalau bhavataḥ śuddhā eva tu suptā jñānākalatāṃ gatāḥ prabuddhāstu / pravibhinnakatipayātmakavedyavido mantra ucyante

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v341] When the whole knowable is divided, the lords of mantras and the great lords arise; when it is both divided and undivided, the path up to Sadāśiva arises, culminating in the supreme Lord.

[tal-a15-v342] As the expansion of difference dissolves, those powers gradually expand and, mutually mixed, become the triad of tvaras; then, with difference dissolved, they go beyond it.

[tal-a15-v343] The triad of lotuses together with unmanā becomes the seat, as the powers take it up out of a desire to cut away their mutual difference.

[tal-a15-v344] Indeed, the divisions of power, its possessor, and so forth become worthy of worship, because from the very first point of the dissolution of difference each bears its own proper form.

[tal-a15-v345] They bear a threefoldness, and that threefoldness of theirs is clearly perceived because of the possible impurity of the knowable and the mutual mixture they acquire.

[tal-a15-v346] Not arriving at a clearly threefold state as before, but ready to devour the very act of cutting mutual difference, that consciousness, whose essence is freedom alone, is declared to be Kālakarṣiṇī.

[tal-a15-v347] She again draws time back from herself and also projects it outward; therefore she is declared Saṃkarṣiṇī, and this is her true being among these Mothers.

[tal-a15-v348] True nature, being, and attainment among the Mothers are to be understood in this way; in those world-generating powers, the supreme reality is indeed freedom alone.

[tal-a15-v349] This worshippable reality, consisting of willing, knowing, and acting, is worthy of worship because it is unlimited; even all directions of limitation are gathered within it.

[tal-a15-v350] Here the non-conceptual does not attain worshippability, nor does a mere single concept where many attributes are involved; therefore the attribute that gathers in that many attributes is required.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-bhinne tvakhile vedye mantreśāstanmaheśāstu / bhinnābhinne tadiyān suśivānto@dhvoditaḥ prete tā eva galati bhedaprasare kramaśo vikāsamāyāntyaḥ / anyonyāsaṃkīrṇāstvarātrayaṃ galitabhedikāstu tataḥ padmatrayyaunmanasī tadidaṃ syādāsanatvena / tā evānyonyātmakabhedāvacchedanājihāsutayā kila śaktitadvadādiprabhidā pūjyatvamāyātāḥ / bhedagalanādyakoṭerārabhya yato nijaṃ nijaṃ rūpam bibhrati tāstu tritvaṃ tāsāṃ sphuṭameva lakṣyeta / saṃbhāvyavedyakāluṣyayogato@nyonyalabdhasaṃkarataḥ prāk prasphuṭaṃ tribhāvaṃ nāgacchannatra tu tathā na / anyonyātmakabhedāvacchedanakalanasaṃgrasiṣṇutayā / svātantryamātrasārā saṃvitsā kālakarṣiṇī kathitā saiva ca bhūyaḥ svasmātsaṃkarṣati kālamiha bahiṣkurute / saṃkarṣiṇīti kathitā mātṛṣveteṣu sadbhāvaḥ tattvaṃ sattā prāptirmātṛṣu meyo@nayā saṃśca / viśvajananīṣu śaktiṣu paramārtho hi svatantratāmātram eṣaṇavidikriyātmakametatpūjyaṃ yato@navacchinnam / yasminsarvāvacchedadiśo@pi syuḥ samākṣiptāḥ avikalpamiha na yāti hi pūjyatvaṃ naca vikalpa ekatra / bahavo dharmāstasmād yo dharmastāvato dharmān

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v351] That which draws in all attributes is established there as supreme, while all others stand lower; such is the principle of supreme Bhairava worship in the great rite of the revered Ḍāmara.

[tal-a15-v352] The glorious Śambhu himself, well pleased, taught this to me: in the external rite one should worship also in the triad of lotuses.

[tal-a15-v353] The teaching of the instructors is that the retinue multitude ends with the weapon mantra, and the fivefold group of vidyā-limbs is placed in the directions of Agni, Īśa, the demons, Vāyu, and the intermediate quarters.

[tal-a15-v354] Here one should likewise place the limbs of Śakti and the limbs of Śiva; again in the pair, place the weapon mantra in the four directions, and in the middle place the mantra called Locana.

[tal-a15-v355] On the eight petals place a pair of octads beginning with Aghorā, according to its own tradition; likewise arrange groups of twelve, six, and four, mixed and distributed two by two.

[tal-a15-v356] One should worship in every way as a doubled enclosure; then, in order, worship the world guardians with their weapons in their own ten directions.

[tal-a15-v357] Thus, abiding in identity with the goddesses up to the trident, standing here and offering the universe, one should satisfy the host of deities.

[tal-a15-v358] Then one should perform recitation, ten times for each mantra; because each is threefold in nature and yet non-different, this holds in all respects.

[tal-a15-v359] Remembering the mantra circle like fire in the navel, heart, throat, palate, and upper center, one should there burn the universe and accomplish the oblation.

[tal-a15-v360] When the act of initiation is to be performed, by whichever path the teacher desires to carry it out, he should first and primarily apply that path in the body.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ākṣipati tatra rūḍhaḥ sarvotkṛṣṭo@dharasthitāstvanye / iti bhairavaparapūjātattvaṃ śrīḍāmare mahāyāge svayameva suprasannaḥ śrīmān śaṃbhurmamādikṣat / bāhyayāge tu padmānāṃ tritaye@pi prapūjayet astrāntaṃ parivāraughamiti no daiśikāgamaḥ / agnīśarakṣovāyvantadikṣu vidyāṅgapañcakam śaktyaṅgāni śivāṅgāni tathaivātra punardvaye / astraṃ nyasyeccaturdikkaṃ madhye locanasaṃjñakam patrāṣṭake@ṣṭakayugamaghorādeḥ svayāmalam / tathā dvādaśakaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ catuṣkaṃ miśritaṃ dviśaḥ sarvaśo dviguṇādītthamāvṛtitvena pūjayet / lokapālāṃstataḥ sāstrānsvadikṣu daśasu kramāt itthaṃ triśūlaparyantadevītādātmyavṛttitaḥ / tiṣṭhannatrārpayanviśvaṃ tarpayeddevatāgaṇam tato japaṃ prakurvīta pratimantraṃ dvipañcadhā / ekaikasya tryātmakatvādabhedāccāpi sarvaśaḥ nābhihṛtkaṇṭhatālūrdhvakuṇḍe jvalanavatsmaran / mantracakraṃ tatra viśvaṃ jvahvansaṃpādayeddhutim dīkṣākarmaṇi kartavye dīkṣāṃ yenādhvanā guruḥ / cikīrṣurdeha evādau bhūyastaṃ mukhyato@rpayet

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v361] Remembering the trident extending from the root up to the twelve-end-point, with its tip forward, and reaching the tip of the circle of goddesses while abandoning sequence, one attains the state of moving in space.

[tal-a15-v362] This khecarī fills everything from the root-support up to the top of the space at the end of the twelve; she is called khecarī because she moves and abides in space and feeds on the nectar of space.

[tal-a15-v363] From that Śāmbhava trident one should reduce by four finger-widths for the Śākta, and from that again for the Āṇava; thus that triad of tridents is established.

[tal-a15-v364] For one whose self is offered to the higher and higher circles of goddesses on that triad of tridents, what is not born, what is not known, or what is not done?

[tal-a15-v365] Alternatively, one should worship each single goddess or each mantra in a lotus, varying the worship according to paired union, limbs, faces, and other options of being or non-being.

[tal-a15-v366] In this way, having made one's own consciousness Śiva from the level of breath up to the level of space through the yoga of worship, one should then perform the external rite.

[tal-a15-v367] When external worship is made primary and is aimed at powers and the like, internal worship is for purification; otherwise the worshipper remains a bound soul.

[tal-a15-v368] But whoever is turned away from powers and the like and worships the Lord outwardly for the sake of rising into the inner great worship, that person is fulfilled by that very means.

[tal-a15-v369] After performing the inner worship, one should take grain and the like consecrated with the weapon-mantra, throw it in the directions to remove obstacles, and then gather it back toward the Īśāna direction.

[tal-a15-v370] Inspection, sprinkling, striking and nourishing, and covering are purifications that are common in the doctrine of Triśiras.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-dvādaśāntamidaṃ prāgraṃ triśūlaṃ mūlataḥ smaran / devīcakrāgragaṃ tyaktakramaḥ khecaratāṃ vrajet mūlādhārāddviṣaṭkāntavyomāgrāpūraṇātmikā / khecarīyaṃ khasaṃcārasthitibhyāṃ khāmṛtāśanāt amuṣmācchāmbhavācchūlāddhrāsayeccaturaṅgulam / śākte tato@pyāṇave tattriśūlatritayaṃ sthitam tattriśūlatrayordhvordhvadevīcakrārpitātmakaḥ / kiṃ kiṃ na jāyate kiṃ vā na vetti na karoti vā ekaikāmathavā devīṃ mantraṃ vā padmagaṃ yajet / yāmalaikyāṅgavaktrādisadasattāvikalpataḥ itthaṃ prāṇādvyomapadaparyantaṃ cetanaṃ nijam / śivībhāvyārcanāyogāttato bāhyaṃ vidhiṃ caret bahiryāgasya mukhyatve siddhyādiparikalpite / antaryāgaḥ saṃskriyāyai hyanyathārcayitā paśuḥ yastu siddhyādivimukhaḥ sa bahiryajati prabhum / antarmahāyāgarūḍhyai tayaivāsau kṛtārthakaḥ kṛtvāntaryāgamādāya dhānyādyastreṇa mantritam / dikṣu kṣipedvighnanude saṃhṛtyaiśīṃ diśaṃ nayet nirīkṣaṇaṃ prokṣaṇaṃ ca tāḍanāpyāyane tathā / viguṇṭhanaṃ ca saṃskārāḥ sādhārāstriśiromate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v371] One should consecrate cow urine, cow dung, curd, milk, and ghee with the faces ending in the upper one and with the six limbs, and sprinkle with this kuśa-water.

[tal-a15-v372] One should sprinkle the ground and set aside the remainder of the pañcagavya for the disciple; where the five cow products are in this kuśa-water, that is called pañcagavya.

[tal-a15-v373] In the scripture, pañcagavya-water is said to remove external impurity; for when ordinary impurity has been removed, one may then deal with the inner impurity.

[tal-a15-v374] To burn away impurity, one must resort to non-ordinary means such as mantra; one should remember the goddess, ending with phāṭ, who extends from earth up to Śiva.

[tal-a15-v375] One should throw a handful of flowers into the middle and likewise offer incense, fragrance, liquor, and so on in the center of the worship-ground; by that the support is quickly empowered.

[tal-a15-v376] The entire circle of deities is conceived as presiding there, on the stalk of Ananta, on the petals beginning with Dharma, and on the pericarp of true knowledge.

[tal-a15-v377] In the sixfold arising, one should worship Gaṇeśa of Īśāna, placed there, with fragrance, flowers, and the like for the calming of obstacles; having worshipped him, one should dismiss him.

[tal-a15-v378] After the missing portion of the text: then one should take the jar, filled with supremely fragrant liquid substances.

[tal-a15-v379] The jar, worshipped and anointed with the root mantra, should be consecrated one hundred times; if the weapon-worship was not done earlier, the water-pot should be consecrated with the sword-mantra.

[tal-a15-v380] One should worship that jar in the Īśāna direction together with the vessel placed on its left; then, taking position in the solar direction, one should worship the world-lords together with their weapons.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-gomūtragomayadadhikṣīrājyaṃ mantrayenmukhaiḥ / ūrdhvāntairaṅgaṣaṭkena kuśāmbvetena cokṣayet bhūmiṃ śeṣaṃ ca śiṣyārthaṃ sthāpayetpañcagavyakam / pañca gavyāni yatrāsminkuśāmbuni taducyate pañcagavyaṃ jalaṃ śāstre bāhyāśuddhivimardakam / laukikyāmaviśuddhau hi mṛditāyāmathāntarīm aśuddhiṃ dagdhumāstheyaṃ mantrādi yadalaukikam / phādināntāṃ smareddevīṃ pṛthivyādiśivāntagām puṣpāñjaliṃ kṣipenmadhye dhūpagandhāsavādi ca / tathaiva dadyādyāgaukomadhye tenāśu vigraham samastaṃ devatācakramadhiṣṭhātṛ prakalpyate / anantanāle dharmādipatre sadvaidyakarṇike ṣaḍutthe gandhapuṣpādyairgaṇeśaṃ hyaiśagaṃ yajet / atthitaṃ vighnasaṃśāntyai pūjayitvā visarjayet ................................................. / ................................................. / / tataḥ kumbhaṃ parāmodidravadravyaprapūritam pūjitaṃ carcitaṃ mūlamanunā mantrayecchatam / asinā karkarīṃ pūrvamastrayāgo na cetkṛtaḥ tamaiśānyāṃ yajetkumbhaṃ vāmasthakalaśānvitam / tataḥ sauradigāśrityā sāstrāṃllokeśvarānyajet

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v381] After worshipping them with offerings of fragrance, flowers, and so on according to rule and preceded by mantra, the disciple, holding the sword-vessel in hand, pours down a stream.

[tal-a15-v382] The guru, holding the jar in hand, should follow while saying this: 'O Śakra, by you, in your own direction, obstacles must be calmed.'

[tal-a15-v383] One must remain attentive until the end of the rite, by Śiva's command; but in a three-syllable name mostly belonging to Nirṛti, only a single 'bhoḥ' should be used.

[tal-a15-v384] One should remove it because this mantra is spoken as bound by meter; then that jar should be placed in the Īśāna direction upon the scattered offerings.

[tal-a15-v385] Now the weapon-vessel should be placed in the south, in relation to the pot, and the group of mantras, strengthened by absorption in the pot's water, is to be used.

[tal-a15-v386] Meditating on the mantra-group as pure light, he should nourish the whole rite; therefore the guru should worship the entire assembly of mantras in the pot.

[tal-a15-v387] Using the previous method, he should employ the weapon-mantra in the karkarī vessel to drive away obstacles; then the guru should worship in the middle of the house on a fragrant diagram.

[tal-a15-v388] He may worship the mantra-deity as the triad, or in a yāmala form, or as a single unity; then, for the fire rite, he should prepare the fire-pit.

[tal-a15-v389] Through contemplation, the fire-pit—arising in an unprecedented way from resolve and the recitation of pure mantras—is understood to be Śiva's power of action.

[tal-a15-v390] Indeed, the supreme consecration can occur even without other ritual sequences, whether in the body, on the altar-ground, in the liṅga, in a vessel, or in water or fire.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-gandhapuṣpopahārādyairvidhinā mantrapūrvakam / tataḥ śiṣyo@sikalaśīhasto dhārāṃ prapātayan guruṇā kumbhahastenānuvrajyo vadatā tvidam / bho bhoḥ śakra tvayā svasyāṃ diśi vighnapraśāntaye sāvadhānena karmāntaṃ bhavitavyaṃ śivājñayā / tryakṣare nirṛtiprāye nāmni bhoḥśabdamekakam apāsayedyato mantraśchandobaddho@yamīritaḥ / tata aiśyāṃ diśi sthāpyaḥ sa kumbho vikiropari dakṣiṇe cāstravārdhānī sthāpyā kumbhasya sāṃpratam / kumbhasthāmbusamāpattivṛṃhitaṃ mantravṛndakam tejomātrātmanā dhyātaṃ sarvamāpyāyayedvidhim / ataḥ kumbhe mantragaṇaṃ sarvaṃ saṃpūjayedguruḥ pūrveṇa vidhināstraṃ ca karkaryāṃ vighnanudyajet / madhyegṛhaṃ tato gandhamaṇḍale pūjayedguruḥ trikaṃ yāmalataikyābhyāmekaṃ vā mantradaivatam / agnikāryavidhānāya tataḥ kuṇḍaṃ prakalpayet śuddhamantrādisaṃjalpasaṃkalpotthamapūrvakam / śivasya yā kriyāśaktistatkuṇḍamiti bhāvanāt paramaḥ khalu saṃskāro vināpyanyaiḥ kriyākramaiḥ / evaṃ dehe sthaṇḍile vā liṅge pātre jale@nale

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v391] In flowers and so on, and even in a child, the primary consecration is that grounded in recognition of Śiva-nature; this is taught in the Yogasañcāra by the Supreme Lord.

[tal-a15-v392] In the fourteenfold range—in being, in flower, incense, food offering, lamp, recitation, and likewise in fire offering—Caṇḍikā is present everywhere.

[tal-a15-v393] She offers into the fire, recites, worships, laughs, and moves; in eating and in sexual union, that same goddess, dwelling in the body, is the doer of all actions.

[tal-a15-v394] But for those who do not rest in that firmly established awareness, a gradual method is taught so that this realization may be accomplished.

[tal-a15-v395] One should clearly remember: 'I am Śiva, consisting of mantra; my resolves are of that same nature; and the fire-pit, fire, and so on arise from Śiva.'

[tal-a15-v396] For this very reason, even there, depending on whether firmness or lack of firmness is seen—while the rite is being performed or after it is done—the consecration may be slight or great.

[tal-a15-v397] Just as someone lacking natural insight may at first grasp a sentence through skill gained by practice, so too it should be understood in this case.

[tal-a15-v398] Drawing, sprinkling, striking, smearing, tracing the axle-circle, and the consecrations of spreading, enclosure, and seat—these ten acts pertaining to the fire-pit are performed by means of the weapon-mantra.

[tal-a15-v399] The center is taken with two darbha blades, the walls are covered with kuśa, upward lines are drawn on the three east-facing lines, and kuśa is also placed outside.

[tal-a15-v400] The auspicious creeper and the square are made, the worship and seat of the ten world-lords are arranged, and the fire-pit is established and protected by the power of the weapon-fire.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-puṣpādiṣu śiśau mukhyaḥ saṃskāraḥ śivatādṛśe / uktaṃ śrīyogasaṃcāre tathāhi parameśinā caturdaśavidhe bhūte puṣpe dhūpe nivedane / dīpe jape tathā home sarvatraivātra caṇḍikā juhoti japati preddhe pūjayedvihasedvrajet / āhāre maithune saiva dehasthā karmakāriṇī tādṛśīṃ ye tu no rūḍhāṃ saṃvittimadhiśerate / akramāttatprasiddhyarthaṃ kramiko vidhirucyate ahaṃ śivo mantramayaḥ saṃkalpā me tadātmakāḥ / tajjaṃ ca kuṇḍavahnyādi śivātmeti sphuṭaṃ smaret ata eva hi tatrāpi dārḍhyādārḍhyāvalokanāt / kriyamāṇe kṛte vāpi saṃskriyālpetarāpivā yathāhi kaścitpratibhādaridro@bhyāsapāṭavāt / vākyaṃ gṛhṇāti ko@pyādau tathātrāpyavabudhyatām ullekhasekakuṭṭanalepacaturmārgamakṣavṛtiparikalanam / staraparidhiviṣṭarasthitisaṃskārā daśāstrataḥ kuṇḍagatāḥ madhyagrahaṇaṃ darbhadvayena kuśasaṃvṛtiśca bhittīnām / prāṅmukharekhātritayordhvarekhikāḥ kuśasamāvṛtiśca bahiḥ śastalatāścaturaśraṃ daśalokeśārcanāsanavidhiśca / sadmāsādanamastrāgnitejasā rakṣaṇaṃ ca kuṇḍasya

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v401] The purposes are to enable the ground to support Śiva's fire and to remove obstacles; then, when the fire-pit has been worshiped, it should be clearly contemplated as the power of action.

[tal-a15-v402] One should install either Mātṛkā or Mālinī in the form of resolve; the triangle, which is the creative abode of the goddess of resolve, is of the nature of action.

[tal-a15-v403] There one should agitate the seed-drop of knowledge three times and place it; knowledge, stirred by will, becomes active in the level of reflective action.

[tal-a15-v404] When it is firmly established and blazes forth, clear with the five limbs beginning with knowing, one should offer an oblation once with each of those five limbs.

[tal-a15-v405] By that much, the fire becomes purified of all consecrations beginning with birth; that five-limbed form indeed has the nature of earth and so on, bearing qualities such as hardness.

[tal-a15-v406] Bearing powers within the fire, it should perform the rites beginning with conception; then it becomes the womb containing the circle of the good goddesses of the whole path and the supreme-and-non-supreme goddess.

[tal-a15-v407] Remembering, and by the power of the full oblation, he should complete the consecrations of the fire; thus the fire blazes with the splendor of true resolve united with the lords of mantra.

[tal-a15-v408] Through identity with that Śiva-resolve, the fire becomes of Śiva-nature; this is the truth of consecration, as the revered Śambhu revealed it to me.

[tal-a15-v409] I have already shown this, so let the pure-minded examine it. Here are those who object, saying it is like the consecration of a child.

[tal-a15-v410] They argue that consecrating fire would require another fire, and so on, leading to infinite regress. In this guru's teaching, that objection is baseless and refuted.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-bhūmeḥ śivāgnidhṛtyai śaktirvighnāpasāraṇaṃ cārthāḥ / tatastu pūjite kuṇḍe kriyāśaktitayā sphuṭam mātṛkāṃ mālinīṃ vāpi nyasyetsaṃkalparūpiṇīm / saṃkalpadevyā yatsṛṣṭidhāma tryaśraṃ kriyātmakam jñānaśukrakaṇaṃ tatra triḥ prakṣobhya vinikṣipet / icchātaḥ kṣubhitaṃ jñānaṃ vimarśātmakriyāpade rūḍhaṃ jñatvādipañcāṅgavispaṣṭaṃ jājvalītyalam / tenāṅgapañcakaireva hutiṃ dadyātsakṛtsakṛt janmādyakhilasaṃskāraśuddho@gnistāvatā bhavet / pañcāṅgameva pṛthvyādirūpaṃ kaṭhinatādikāḥ śaktīrdadhadvahnigatāḥ kuryādgarbhādikāḥ kriyāḥ / tato@khilādhvasaddevīcakragarbhāṃ parāparām smaranpūrṇāhutivaśātpūrayedagnisaṃskriyāḥ / tathā mantreśayuksatyasaṃkalpamahasā jvalan vahnistacchivasaṃkalpatādātmyācchivatātmakaḥ / ityetatsaṃskriyātattvaṃ śrīśaṃbhurme nyarūpayat mayāpi darśitaṃ śuddhabuddhayaḥ praviviñcatām / tenātra ye codayanti yathā bālasya saṃskriyā bahnau vahnestathānyatretyanavasthaiva saṃskṛteḥ / te nirutthānavihatā naye@smingurudarśane

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v411] Once the fire has arisen and been consecrated in the Shaiva way, one should worship the mass of sound and Malini as the two parents, and then dismiss them to their own pure abode.

[tal-a15-v412] One should take a portion of the pure fire and set it apart for the oblation. Or, alternatively, one may draw the flame from the fire with the left breath and the heart mantra.

[tal-a15-v413] Bringing it to unity with the fire of consciousness, one should cast the consecrated element with the right side. Indeed, the true seeing is a firm identification: 'I am Shiva.'

[tal-a15-v414] Consecration is the true principle for everything. Therefore, for whatever impurity belongs to anything, one should offer nine oblations, or nine together with the self.

[tal-a15-v415] The consecration should be made to Shiva-fire with a mantra beginning with Om and ending with Svaha, in the fire understood as the shared form of Shiva-consciousness. Then:

[tal-a15-v416] As before, one should install the support and what rests on it, and also the circle of goddesses. Then the guru should, in order, see the ladle and the spoon as facing downward.

[tal-a15-v417] They are to be worshipped as Shiva and Shakti. Thus is their consecration performed. Apart from seeing that principle, consecration has no other life.

[tal-a15-v418] Thus, as the Shri Purva states, the lord of the ladle and the rest did not consecrate in that way. Then the guru, using sesame, forms the doe mudra by controlling the middle, ring, and thumb fingers.

[tal-a15-v419] Having formed the mudra, one should satisfy the root mantra with a hundred ladles of ghee, the limbs and faces with a sixth part, and the rest with a tenth part.

[tal-a15-v420] Even a thousandfold offering may be made for satisfaction, according to one's means. But if, even when means are available, one is seized by greed and gives priority to outer things—
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-jāte@gnau saṃskṛte śaive śabdarāśiṃ ca mālinīm / pitarau pūjayitvā svaṃ śuddhaṃ dhāma visarjayet śuddhāgnerbhāgamādāya carvarthaṃ sthāpayetpṛthak / athavāgneḥ śikhāṃ vāmaprāṇenādāya hṛjjuṣā cidagninaikyamānīya kṣipeddakṣeṇa saṃskṛtām / śiva ityabhimānena dṛḍhena hi vilokanam sarvasya saṃskriyā tattvaṃ tattasmai yadyato@malam / navāhutīratho dadyānnavātmasahitena tu śivāgnaye tārapūrvaṃ svāhāntaṃ saṃskriyā bhavet / śivacaitanyasāmānyavyoparūpe@nale tataḥ prāgvadādhāramādheyaṃ devīcakraṃ ca yojayet / sruvaṃ srucaṃ ca saṃpaśyedadhovaktrau kramādguruḥ śivaśaktitayābhyarcyau tathetthaṃ saṃskriyānayoḥ / tattvasaṃdarśanānnānyatsaṃskārasyāsti jīvitam iti vaktuṃ sruvādīśaḥ śrīpūrve na samaskarot / tatastilairmṛgīṃ madhyānāmāṅguṣṭhavaśādguruḥ kṛtvā mūlaṃ tarpayet śatenājyasruvaistathā / aṅgavaktraṃ ṣaḍaṃśena śeṣāṃścāpi daśāṃśataḥ sahasrādikahomo@pi tṛptyai vittānusārataḥ / sati vitte@pi lobhādigrasto bāhyapradhānatām

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v421] By promoting outer display and making consciousness secondary, such a person does not receive the descent of power. It is said in the Svacchanda Tantra that even one initiated in that state does not attain liberation.

[tal-a15-v422] But then, what fruit does the rite performed in his initiation have? To this the knowers of Agama scripture reply: at that time, the mantras, made of Vama power—

[tal-a15-v423] The mantras bind him firmly in the great prison-house of worldly existence. But their grace-bestowing power, when kindled by the guru, is different.

[tal-a15-v424] One should purify the disinterested transgressive act prescribed in one's own scripture. Then, by placing things above and below, one makes an arrangement beautiful in its mutual facing.

[tal-a15-v425] Taking the spoon and ladle as Shiva and Shakti, filled with the nectar of ghee, one does so through the method of uniting mind, breath, and body into one.

[tal-a15-v426] With care, one should place the left hand holding the spoon handle and the supported right hand below the throat, pressing them firmly.

[tal-a15-v427] One should place the spoon below, directing the breath upward and upward until the end of the twelve, into the fire of awareness, from the moon circle.

[tal-a15-v428] As the supreme, delightful nectar falls from the tip of the spoon, one should cast into the fire, at the mouth of mantra, an oblation ending with Vaushat.

[tal-a15-v429] The awareness above is reflected in the fire pit. The fire is breath, the spoon and ladle are its instruments, and the ghee is the essence of consciousness in the form of intention.

[tal-a15-v430] Knowing thus from the beginning the fire pit, spoon, ladle, ghee, and mantras, one should contain them firmly in the fire of awareness at the twelvefold end and cast the full oblation.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-prathayaṃścidguṇībhāvācchaktipātaṃ na vindati / uktaṃ svacchandatantre taddīkṣito@pi na mokṣabhāk nanu yattasya dīkṣāyāṃ kṛtaṃ karmāsya kiṃ phalam / tatrāhurgamaśāstrajñā vāmāśaktimayāstadā mantrā badhnanti taṃ samyagbhavakārāmahāgṛhe / yā tvanugrāhikā śaktisteṣāṃ sā gurudīpitā śodhayeta svaśāstrasthaniṣkāmollaṅghanakriyām / tata ūrdhvādharanyāsādanyonyaunmukhyasundaram sruksruvaṃ śivaśaktyātmādāyājyāmṛtapūritam / samacittaprāṇatanuraikātmyavidhiyogataḥ vāmaṃ srugdaṇḍagaṃ hastaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ sopayāmakam / kaṇṭhādhogaṃ vinikṣipya dṛḍhamāpīḍya yatnavān adhaḥ kuryātsrucaṃ prāṇamūrdhvordhvaṃ saṃniyojayan / yāvaddviṣaṭkaparyante bodhāgnau candracakrataḥ srugagrātparamaṃ hlādi patedamṛtamuttamam / tāvadvahnau mantramukhe vauṣaḍantāṃ hutiṃ kṣipet ya ūrdhve kila saṃbodhaḥ kuṇḍe sa pratibimbitaḥ / vahniḥ prāṇaḥ sruksruvau ca snehaḥ saṃkalpacidrasaḥ itthaṃ jñātvāditaḥ kuṇḍasruksruvājyamanūnbhṛśam / dvādaśāntavibodhāgnau ruddhvā pūrṇāhutiṃ kṣipet

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v431] Just as a swan rises into the sky while its reflection sinks in the water, so too this method works here.

[tal-a15-v432] Natural and stable, fluid and luminous, moving and space—so too Maya, Bindu, the Self, Nada, Shakti, and likewise Shiva.

[tal-a15-v433] Thus the levels below, from earth to root, are arranged in the pervaded-pervader order, and so is the person.

[tal-a15-v434] So ignorance, desire, niyati, time, maya, kala, atom, vidya, ishvara, sada-shiva, and shakti-kundalini are listed.

[tal-a15-v435] The pervading one should be joined in name, while in exhalation at the middle channel junction, as the guru says.

[tal-a15-v436] This is said in the Trishiras tantra in the description of supreme purpose; then by fire purified with previously established other mantras.

[tal-a15-v437] The offering, or the accomplished one, is simultaneous with disciples' oblation; heroic or worldly substances may be added by wish.

[tal-a15-v438] On success of the offering, all acts come from heart-mantra union; then taking the offering, the guru fills it by royal authority.

[tal-a15-v439] Having made a ladle or spoon according to enjoyment or liberation, there are triads of gods, powers, and yantras.

[tal-a15-v440] Reciting the seventh mother-presence in order, one by one, with svaha and nectar syllable, offer the ghee remainder into the fire.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-yathā yathā hi gaganamutpatetkalahaṃsakaḥ / jale binbaṃ bruḍatyasya tathetyatrāpyayaṃ vidhiḥ svābhāvikaṃ sthiraṃ caiva dravaṃ dīptaṃ calaṃ nabhaḥ / māyā bindustathaivātmā nādaḥ śaktiḥ śivastathā itthaṃ vyāpyavyāpakato vibhedyābhyantarāntam / tadadhaḥsthāni pṛthvyādimūlāntāni tathā pumān avidyārāganiyatikālamāyākalāstathā / aṇurvidyā tadīśeśau sādākhyaṃ śaktikuṇḍalī vyāpinī samanaunmanyaṃ tato@nāmani yojayet / recakastho madhyanāḍīsandhividgururityadaḥ proktaṃ traiśirase tantre parayojanavarṇane / tataḥ prāksthāpitānyastamantrasaṃskṛtavahninā caruḥ sādhyo@thavā śiṣyairhomena samakālakaḥ / carau ca vīradravyāṇi laukikānyathavecchayā carusiddhau samastāśca kriyā hṛnmantrayogataḥ / tataścaruṃ samādāya gururājyena pūritām srucaṃ sruvaṃ vā kṛtvaiva bhuktimuktyanusārataḥ / devānāmatha śaktīnāṃ yantrāṇāṃ tu trayaṃ trayam saptamaṃ mātṛsadbhāvaṃ kramādekaikaśaḥ paṭhan / svā ityamṛtavarṇena vahnau hutvājyaśeṣakam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v441] In the offering, as fire-form, one should offer that again; thus eater and eaten are unified in chewing fire.

[tal-a15-v442] By svaha reflection with mantra, the supreme nondual arises; this is the meeting-purification of the offering, whose eater presides.

[tal-a15-v443] The supreme essence of the enjoyable dances carefully; through equal unified falling, eater and enjoyed are one.

[tal-a15-v444] Elsewhere, from meeting and union, it is thus called; on the ground, offer a share of pot and gourd.

[tal-a15-v445] By share in fire, mantra satisfaction is twofold for disciple and self; thus the prescribed duty is declared by the lord.

[tal-a15-v446] To purify disciples by shaktipata order, one should go out; there, five cow products, offering, and ten cleansing are used.

[tal-a15-v447] That fall is auspicious toward east, northeast, or upward; inauspicious elsewhere; there, weapon oblation of eight hundred should be.

[tal-a15-v448] With eyes bound by mantra-cloth and steady, hearts become non-other through strength and restraint.

[tal-a15-v449] The guru, with palm filled with pearls, gems, and flowers, enters, seats them at the ground edge on their knees.

[tal-a15-v450] They should throw that palm; disciples with purified selves refill the palm again, and lightly use cloth.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-carau hetyagnirūpeṇa juhuyāttatpunaḥ punaḥ / bhojyabhojakacarvagnyoritthamekānusandhitaḥ svāhāpratyavamarśātsyātsamantrādadvayaṃ param / eṣa saṃpātasaṃskāraścarorbhoktā hyadhiṣṭhitaḥ bhogyasya paramaṃ sāraṃ bhogyaṃ narnarti yatnataḥ / samamekānusandhānātpātato bhoktṛbhogyayoḥ anyo@nyatra ca saṃpātātsaṃgamāccetthamucyate / sthaṇḍile kubhbhakarkaryorbhāgaṃ bhāgaṃ nivedayet bhāgenāgnau mantratṛptirdvayaṃ śiṣyātmanoratha / itthaṃ vihitakartavyo vijñāpyeśaṃ tadīritaḥ śaktipātakramācchiṣyānsaṃskartuṃ niḥsaredbahiḥ / tatraiṣāṃ pañcagavyaṃ ca caruṃ daśanamārjanam tasya pātaḥ śubhaḥ prācīsaumyaiśāpyordhvadiggataḥ / aśubho@nyatra tatrāstrahomo@pyaṣṭaśataṃ bhavet netramantritasadvastrabaddhanetrānacañcalān / ananyahṛdayībhūtānbalāditthaṃ nirodhataḥ muktāratnādikusumasaṃpūrṇāñjalikānguruḥ / praveśya sthaṇḍilopāgra upaveśyaiva jānubhiḥ prakṣepayedañjaliṃ taṃ taiḥ śiṣyairbhāvitātmabhiḥ / añjali punarāpūrya teṣāṃ lāghavataḥ paṭam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v451] He too should restrain sight; the disciple suddenly sees in the place raised by mantra power.

[tal-a15-v452] Through possession, the disciple attains that-nature, as a red heart indeed sees beloved qualities by itself.

[tal-a15-v453] Thus the shaktipata-purified one sees mantra presence, since the eye and other senses are cooperators in such a state.

[tal-a15-v454] Even before truth is extremely unseen, fitness would arise; indeed, placed mantra is in body, water, and land.

[tal-a15-v455] Seeing images and so on, they know presence and absence, marked by placed mantra ray and auspicious elements.

[tal-a15-v456] As if trembling, those consciousness-senses with cooperators; then in his right hand is shining, all-path-filled.

[tal-a15-v457] The guru should worship the bond-burning circle of mantras with the left hand, then place that hand of the disciple on the head of the disciple whose body contains the whole continuum of paths.

[tal-a15-v458] He should place in order on all the limbs and touch the disciple with that very hand; this is taught in the Dīkṣottara as done with a hand shining with a cascade of flames.

[tal-a15-v459] By the bestowal of the Śiva-hand he is made a samaya-initiate; while still alive he becomes fit for knowledge, and he attains union in the level of Īśvara.

[tal-a15-v460] But in the Śrīdevyāthāmala it is taught in a circle with an eight-spoked inner trident, with Bhairava at the navel and Aghora and the other eight forming it.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-dṛśornivārayetso@pi śiṣyo jhaṭiti paśyati / jhaṭityālokite māntraprabhāvollāsite sthale tadāveśavaśācchiṣyastanmayatvaṃ prapadyate / yathā hi raktahṛdayastāṃstānkāntāguṇānsvayam paśyatyevaṃ śaktipātasaṃskṛto mantrasannidhim / cakṣurādīndriyāṇāṃ hi sahakāriṇi tādṛśe satyatyantamadṛṣṭe prāgapi jāyeta yogyatā / kṛtaprajñā hi vinyastamantraṃ dehaṃ jalaṃ sthalam pratimādi ca paśyanto viduḥ saṃnidhyasaṃnidhī / nyastamantrāṃśusubhagātkiṃcidbhūtādimudritāḥ trasyantīveti tattaccidakṣaistatsahakāribhiḥ / tataḥ sa dakṣiṇe haste dīptaṃ sarvādhvapūritam mantracakraṃ yajedvāmapāṇinā pāśadāhakam / taṃ śiṣyasya karaṃ mūrdhni dehanyastādhvasaṃtateḥ nyasyetkrameṇa sarvāṃṅgaṃ tenaivāsya ca saṃspṛśet / uktaṃ dīkṣottare caitajjvālāsaṃpātaśobhinā dattena śivahastena samayī sa vidhīyate / sāyujyamīśvare tattve jīvato@dhītiyogyatā śrīdevyāthāmale tūktamaṣṭārāntastriśūlake / cakre bhairavasannābhāvaghorādyaṣṭakārake

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v461] It is visualized with an outer lower part and a supreme rim, and with a middle trident having supreme and lower aspects, all flame-filled, reddish, and fearsome with whirling Mothers and the praṇava.

[tal-a15-v462] When this is contemplated and seen in the outer hand, one becomes a samaya-initiate; but if agitation of the bonds and the like appears at once, that shows the person is about to depart.

[tal-a15-v463] If he is about to depart, the guru should worship outside that and cast upon the head what separates him from the life-breaths; by this Śiva-hand he clearly becomes a samaya-initiate.

[tal-a15-v464] For that same person, in the future proper separation from the bonds of the levels, he has the status of a son, and the initiating teachers are to join him to the supreme level.

[tal-a15-v465] That same person, knowing the kinds of mantras and the truth of recitation, fire-offering, and the rest, is consecrated first with the liberation vessel and then with the one called Īśvara.

[tal-a15-v466] When consecrated he becomes a sādhaka, and at the end of enjoyment he dissolves into the supreme; endowed with these qualities, one is initiated in the teaching of Śiva.

[tal-a15-v467] One who knows the four-part scriptures, is devoted to the eighteen tantras, and knows the ten tantras and the higher path is appointed as an ācārya.

[tal-a15-v468] In the consecration rite, the best of gurus should perform for the ācārya the joining that begins from earth and ends in liberation.

[tal-a15-v469] By these statements it is said that the samaya-initiate, like a prince, would be authorized everywhere in the three stages beginning with the son stage.

[tal-a15-v470] A son-initiate may be authorized in teacherhood if his joining is equal, but he is not authorized in sādhana when the joining is different.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-bāhyāpare parānemau madhyaśūlaparāpare / jvālākule@ruṇe bhrāmyanmātṛpraṇavabhīṣaṇe cintite tu bahirhaste saṃdṛṣṭe samayī bhavet / pāśastobhādyastu sadya uccikramiṣurasya tam prāṇairviyojakaṃ mūrdhni kṣipetsaṃpūjya tadbahiḥ / anena śivahastena samayī bhavati sphuṭam tasyaiva bhāvividhivattattvapāśaviyojane / putrakatvaṃ sa ca pare tattve yojyastu daiśikaiḥ sa eva mantrajātijño japahomāditattvavit / nirvāṇakalaśenādau tata īśvarasaṃjñinā abhiṣiktaḥ sādhakaḥ syādbhogānte@sya pare layaḥ / etairguṇaiḥ samāyukto dīkṣitaḥ śivaśāsane catuṣpātsaṃhitābhijñastantrāṣṭādaśatatparaḥ / daśatantrātimārgajña ācāryaḥ sa vidhīyate pṛthivīmāditaḥ kṛtvā nirvāṇānte@sya yojanām / abhiṣekavidhau kuryādācāryasya gurūttamaḥ etairvākyairidaṃ coktaṃ samayī rājaputravat / sarvatraivādhikārī syātputrakādipadatraye putrako daiśikatve tu tulyayojaniko bhavet / adhikārī sa na punaḥ sādhane bhinnayojane

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v471] In this tantra, the ācārya is one who has obtained the higher rites through the sequence beginning with samaya; never a Buddhist, Vaiṣṇava, or the like.

[tal-a15-v472] Thus what arose by context has been settled, and now the main topic is taken up again: having performed the Śiva-hand rite, by that the disciple's bonds are burned away.

[tal-a15-v473] Having brought the disciple, through meditative absorption, to the point of rest, the guru then places that child-disciple in the vessel, in the weapon-vessel, in the fire, and in his own self.

[tal-a15-v474] He should have the disciple make prostration, then cast an offering to the beings and Mothers; then, having worshipped Śaṃkara, he should prepare a bed consecrated with the weapon-mantra.

[tal-a15-v475] Having placed the disciple on that bed and installed the mantras, the guru establishes rest in the disciple's heart-wheel and then goes to his twelve-end.

[tal-a15-v476] Through the arising of the twelve vowels the net of kalās becomes diminished; then, on entry, he becomes bright with the sixteen kalās gathered together.

[tal-a15-v477] As the full moon of his own consciousness, he should rest in the heart of the child-disciple until the rising, and then go to the twelve-end.

[tal-a15-v478] He should enter the heart-wheel again in this way; this is the sequence of the sleep rite. When sleep has come, this disciple perceives the stainless moon and sun.

[tal-a15-v479] In the heart-wheel he forcibly joins together the full and the thin moon and sun, and he truly sees the light of the forcibly stainless moon and sun.

[tal-a15-v480] He sees a dream that clearly reveals future good and other outcomes; and it is taught that, having meditated on the full and the thin in the domain of the twelve, this occurs.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-etattantre samayyādikramādāptottarakriyaḥ / ācāryo na punarbauddhavaiṣṇavādiḥ kadācana evaṃ prasaṅgānnirṇītaṃ prakṛtaṃ tu nirūpyate / śivahastavidhiṃ kṛtvā tena saṃpluṣṭapāśakam śiṣyaṃ vidhāya viśrāntiparyantaṃ dhyānayogataḥ / tataḥ kumbhe@strakalaśe vahnau svātmani taṃ śiśum praṇāmaṃ kārayetpaścādbhūtamātṛbaliṃ kṣipet / tataḥ śaṃkaramabhyarcya śayyāmastrābhimantritām kṛtvāsyāṃ śiṣyamāropya nyastamantraṃ vidhāya ca / śiṣyahṛccakraviśrāntiṃ kṛtvā taddvādaśāntagaḥ bhavetkṣīṇakalājālaḥ svaradvādaśakodayāt / tataḥ praveśapracitakalāṣoḍaśakojjvalaḥ saṃpūrṇasvātmaciccandro viśrāmyeddhṛdaye śiśoḥ / svayaṃ vyutthānaparyantaṃ dvādaśāntaṃ tato vrajet punarviśecca hṛccakramitthaṃ nidrāvidhikramaḥ / āyātanidraḥ śiṣyo@sau nirmalau śaśibhāskarau hṛccakre pratisaṃdhatte balātpūrṇakṛśātmakau / haṭhanirmalacandrārkaprakāśaḥ satyamīkṣate svapnaṃ bhāviśubhānyatvasphuṭībhāvanakovidam / uktaṃ ca pūrṇāṃ ca kṛśāṃ dhyātvā dvādaśagocare

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v481] Entering the heart, meditate; the sleeping child, with the guru worshipping Shankara, attains freedom in temple sleep.

[tal-a15-v482] Eat the offering with a friend, then clean the teeth, and sleep with mind fixed in the heart wheel by mantra rays.

[tal-a15-v483] In the morning the guru, having completed daily worship of Shankara, knows the dream-seen meanings of disciple and self from strength and weakness.

[tal-a15-v484] Self-seen strength is not other through awakening excess; in knowledge equality, dream equality would again arise between guru and disciple.

[tal-a15-v485] God, fire, guru, worship cause and utensils are pleasing; woman, wine drinking, and eating of uncooked meat also appear.

[tal-a15-v486] Blood drinking, head cutting, smearing with blood, feces, and urine, and riding pleasing vehicles such as mountain, horse, and elephant.

[tal-a15-v487] For pleasure it would even be; mostly that is declared auspicious; announce it for growth of satisfaction, for joy indeed is the supreme fruit.

[tal-a15-v488] Therefore other inauspicious signs there; from homa of eight hundred, inauspicious is not inauspicious; thus the guru tells the disciples.

[tal-a15-v489] Indeed great effort arises to cut rooted doubt; but for those whose doubt dissolves, dream-power arises.

[tal-a15-v490] Nothing auspicious or inauspicious would be; if thus, from variegation power the sattva self clearly sees from sign only.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-praviśya hṛdaye dhyāye tsuptaḥ svācchandyamāpnuyāt / āyātanidre ca śiśau gururabhyarcya śaṅkaram caruṃ bhuñjīta sasakhā tato@dyāddantadhāvanam / svapyācca mantraraśmīddhahṛccakrārpitamānasaḥ prātarguruḥ kṛtāśeṣanityo@bhyarcitaśaṃkaraḥ / śiṣyātmanoḥ svapnadṛṣṭāvarthau vitte balābalāt svadṛṣṭaṃ balavannānyatsaṃbodhodrekayogataḥ / bodhasāmye punaḥ svapnasāmyaṃ syādguruśiṣyayoḥ devāgnigurutatpūjākāraṇopaskarādikam / hṛdyā strī madyapānaṃ cāpyāmamāṃsasya bhakṣaṇam raktapānaṃ śiraśchedo raktaviṇmūtralepanam / parvatāśvagajaprāyahṛdyayugyādhirohaṇam yatprītyai syādapi prāyastattacchubhamudāhṛtam / taṃ khyāpayettuṣṭivṛddhyai hlādo hi paramaṃ phalam ato@nyadaśubhaṃ tatra homo@ṣṭaśatako@strataḥ / aśubhaṃ nāśubhamiti śiṣyebhyo kathayedguruḥ rūḍhāṃ hi śaṅkāṃ vicchettuṃ yatnaḥ saṃghaṭate mahān / yeṣāṃ tu śaṅkāvilayasteṣāṃ svapnavaśotthitam śubhāśubhaṃ na kiṃcitsyāt syuścetthaṃ citratāvaśāt / sphuṭaṃ paśyati sattvātmā rājaso liṅgamātrataḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v491] Nothing tamasic is his pleasure, pain, auspiciousness, or inauspiciousness; indeed here, how would the one named tamasic be fit in the rite?

[tal-a15-v492] Let no one dispute anywhere indeed; quality is present; even all sattvic action in eating, if tamasic.

[tal-a15-v493] Then what is low, or high is the opposite; even arrived power descent and initiation depend on quality state.

[tal-a15-v494] The variegated self would indeed be composed in chief purpose; then the guru teaches the child mantra-preceded deity worship.

[tal-a15-v495] He would teach and do that, purify him; then the composed guru addresses six places from the heart, brahma and others.

[tal-a15-v496] He would touch the child's breath function; each of eight purifications, purified by knowledge-touch, extends to the heart-first twelve end.

[tal-a15-v497] By destruction of faults from food, seed, state, and so on, one becomes twice-born; full of vasu-veda-named purification, thus the twice-born stands.

[tal-a15-v498] Conception, male-producing, parting, birth, naming, exit, food tasting, tonsure, and the eighth.

[tal-a15-v499] In vow binding and sacrificial, sacred thread and worldly rites, in order: soma-related, cow gift, veda-moon purification, from celibacy.

[tal-a15-v500] Marriage is fifteenth; from there seven cooked sacrifices, eighth-day rites, fortnightly, ancestral offering, and the shravana-agrayana pair.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-na kiṃcittāmasastasya sukhaduḥkhācchubhāśubham / nanvatra tāmaso nāma kathaṃ yogyo vidhau bhavet maiva mā vigrahaṃ kaścitkvacitkasyāpi vai guṇaḥ / sarvasāttvikaceṣṭo@pi bhojane yadi tāmasaḥ kiṃ tataḥ so@dhamaḥ kivāpyutkṛṣṭastadviparyayaḥ / āyātaśaktipāto@pi dīkṣito@pi guṇasthiteḥ vicitrātmā bhavedeva mukhye tvarthe samāhitaḥ / tato guruḥ śiśormantrapūrvakaṃ devatārcanam deśayetsa ca tatkuryātsaṃskuryāttaṃ tato guruḥ / hṛdādicakraṣaṭkasthānbrahmādīn ṣaṭ samāhitaḥ spṛśecchiśoḥ prāṇavṛttyā pratyekaṃ cāṣṭa saṃskriyāḥ / hṛdayādidviṣaṭkāntaṃ bodhasparśapavitritaḥ āhārabījabhāvādidoṣadhvaṃsādbhaveddvijaḥ / vasuvedākhyasaṃskārapūrṇa itthaṃ dvijaḥ sthitaḥ garbhādhānaṃ puṃsavanaṃ sīmanto jātakarma ca / nāma niṣkrāmaṇaṃ cānnapraśaścūḍā tathāṣṭamī vratabandhaiṣṭike maujjībhautike saumikaṃ kramāt / godānamiti vedendusaṃskriyā brahmacaryataḥ pratyudvāhaḥ pañcadaśaḥ sapta pākamakhāstvataḥ / aṣṭakāḥ pārvaṇī śrāddhaṃ śrāvaṇyāgrāyaṇīdvayam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v501] Chaitra and ashvayuja; after them seven oblation sacrifices; placed fire offering, full moon, and seeing.

[tal-a15-v502] Four-month rite, animal binding, with sautramani; these, agnishtoma first, then soma-related and sixteen vajapeya.

[tal-a15-v503] Aptoryama and atiratra; these seven are soma-established; golden-foot sacrifice surrounded by a thousand.

[tal-a15-v504] The thirty-eighth is horse sacrifice; householder rite would be by measure; forest and renunciation rites are considered the fortieth.

[tal-a15-v505] Compassion, forbearance, non-envy, purity, good conduct, auspiciousness, non-miserliness, and non-desire are remembered as this eightfold set of qualities of the self.

[tal-a15-v506] The girdle, staff, skin, lifelong observances, fire worship, twilight rite, and alms are the seven consecrations, and there are also seven vows.

[tal-a15-v507] The Bhauta and Pashupata are two, then the Ganesha and Ganapatya, and with the Unmattaka, sword-edge, and Ghrita-lord observances they make fourteen in all.

[tal-a15-v508] These are remembered as the principal consecrations of vow-binding; in the case of renunciation, the final rite is as if in the womb, and by that one is consecrated.

[tal-a15-v509] Then the person becomes twice-born and fit to attain a share in Rudra; the guru should apply these consecrations in the very sequence of the breath.

[tal-a15-v510] Alternatively, using oblations of sesame and the like preceded by mantra, one uses the formula: Om, the heart, the name, 'I purify, beloved of fire'.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-caitrī cāśvayujī paścāt saptaiva tu havirmakhāḥ / ādheyamagnihotraṃ ca paurṇamāsaḥ sadarśakaḥ cāturmāsyaṃ paśūdbandhaḥ sautrāmaṇyā saha tvamī / agniṣṭomo@tipūrvo@tha sokyyaḥ ṣoḍaśivājapau āptoryāmātirātrau ca saptaitāḥ somasaṃsthitāḥ / hiraṇyapādādimakhaḥ sahasreṇa samāvṛtaḥ aṣṭatriṃśastvaśvamedho gārhasthyamiyatā bhavet / vānasthyapārivrājye ca catvāriṃśadamī matāḥ dayā kṣamānasūyā ca śuddhiḥ satkṛtimaṅgale / akārpaṇyāspṛhe cātmaguṇāṣṭakamidaṃ smṛtam mekhalā daṇḍamajinatryāyuṣe vahnyupāsanam / saṃdhyā bhikṣeti saṃskārāḥ sapta sapta vratāni ca bhauteśapāśupatye dve gāṇeśaṃ gāṇapatyakam / unmattakāsidhārākhyaghṛteśāni caturdaśa ete tu vratabandhasya saṃskārā aṅginaḥ smṛtāḥ / pārivrājyasya garbhe syādantyeṣṭiriti saṃskṛtaḥ dvijo bhavettato yogyo rudrāṃśāpādanāya saḥ / etānprāṇakrameṇaiva saṃskārānyojayedguruḥ athavāhutiyogena tilādyairmantrapūrvakaiḥ / praṇavo hṛdayaṃ nāma śodhayāmyagnivallabhā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v511] Thus, in sequence, with the head and other limbs, again and again: because the twice-born state is truly of the nature of consciousness, characterized by peace and the rest.

[tal-a15-v512] Therefore awareness arises in the state of Rudra through that very sequence, just as gold and other metals, in refining, are transformed by the force of sequence.

[tal-a15-v513] Likewise, as with silver and the rest, in the consecration of awareness within the twice-born state the womb is not the cause; there, one who is of peaceful nature is called twice-born.

[tal-a15-v514] This has been examined by the sage in the Moksha-dharma and elsewhere, and it has also been ascertained by the Lord in scriptures such as the Mukuta.

[tal-a15-v515] Because awareness can arise similarly through similar bodily connection, from the standpoint of common convention, in the Smarta sense the son of two twice-born parents is called twice-born.

[tal-a15-v516] Even seers born of mothers associated with low-caste conditions of mind, speech, or birth had elevated minds; what need, then, of brahminhood alone to be a worthy receptacle?

[tal-a15-v517] For this reason, in this secret scripture that teaches the truth of real meaning, conduct based on birth and similar factors is indeed taught for the Śāmbhava path.

[tal-a15-v518] But the pāśava scriptures are thoroughly of the nature of vāma-śakti, serving accomplishment in creation and related aims, and also serving fear and the arrangement of results under Śambhu.

[tal-a15-v519] For one who has been made twice-born, descent from the twelve-end comes not merely by touch, but by resting in union with one's own self and suddenly descending.

[tal-a15-v520] By the conferring of a Rudra-share, the samaya-initiate becomes consecrated and is thereby fit for study, hearing, daily worship, and service to the guru.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-evaṃ krameṇa mūrdhādyairaṅgairatatpunaḥ punaḥ / yataściddharma evāsau śāntyādyātmā dvijanmatā tena rudratayā saṃvittatkrameṇaiva jāyate / yathā hemādidhātūnāṃ pāke kramavaśādbhavet rajatādi tathā saṃvitsaṃskāre dvijatāntare / yonirna kāraṇaṃ tatra śāntātmā dvija ucyate muninā mokṣadharmādāvetacca pravivecitam / mukuṭādiṣu śāstreṣu devenāpi nirūpitam saṃvido dehasaṃbhedātsadṛśātsadṛśodayāt / bhūmābhiprāyataḥ smārte dvijanmā dvijayoḥ sutaḥ antyajātīyadhīvādijananījanmalābhataḥ / utkṛṣṭacittā ṛṣayaḥ kiṃ brāhmaṇyena bhājanam ata evārthasattattvadeśinyasminna diśyate / rahasyaśāstre jātyādisamācāro hi śāmbhave pāśavāni tu śāstrāṇi vāmaśaktyātmakānyalam / sṛṣṭyāṃcisiddhaye śaṃbhoḥ śaṅkātatphalakḷptaye āpāditadvijatvasya dvādaśānte nijaikyataḥ / sparśamātrānna viśrāntyā jhaṭityevāvarohataḥ rudrāṃśāpādanaṃ yena samayī saṃskṛto bhavet / adhītau śravaṇe nityaṃ pūjāyāṃ gurusevane

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v521] One authorized as a samaya-initiate should worship the Lord under the guru, and the guru should make that person, now given a Rudra-share, hear the samaya-pledges.

[tal-a15-v522] In the Yāmala and related texts of the Goddess, the pledges are set forth as eight groups of eight, including restraint in speech and action, concealment, worship, satiation, and contemplation.

[tal-a15-v523] Striking and deluding, and so on, belong to an eightfold set of pledges expressed in eight ways, forming the unified samaya conduct that reflects the nature of mantra and tantra.

[tal-a15-v524] One should not speak false, harsh, or untrue words, nor engage in fruitless action, harm, or touching another's wife.

[tal-a15-v525] One should not practice pride, hypocrisy, or rites for spirits, poison, and disease, and one should guard one's own mantra, rosary, and knowledge that has the nature of true knowledge.

[tal-a15-v526] One should conceal one's conduct, qualities, hardships, and signs of success, and one should honor the guru, the scripture, the god, the fire, elders in knowledge, women, and the vow.

[tal-a15-v527] According to one's ability, one should worship the guru-lineage and this eightfold group: the poor, the afflicted, ancestors, field-guardians, living beings, and birds.

[tal-a15-v528] One should satiate the cremation-ground host of beings, the goddess of the body, Śiva, Śakti, and likewise the self, as well as the seal that has the form of mantra.

[tal-a15-v529] One should contemplate worldly enjoyment and liberation as taught by the guru, and restrain attachment, hatred, envy, contraction, jealousy, and pride.

[tal-a15-v530] One should strike down those who break the pledges and their wrong practices, as well as the cruel and hostile followers of the bound path, slanderers, and dullards.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-samayyadhikṛto@nyatra guruṇā vibhumarcayet / tamāpāditarudrāṃśaṃ samayān śrāvayedguruḥ aṣṭāṣṭakātmakāndevyāyāmalādau nirūpitān / avādo@karaṇaṃ gūḍhiḥ pūjā tarpaṇabhāvane hananaṃ mohanaṃ ceti samayāṣṭakamaṣṭadhā / svabhāvaṃ mantratantrāṇāṃ samayācāramelakam asatpralāpaṃ paruṣamanṛtaṃ nāṣṭadhā vadet / aphalaṃ ceṣṭitaṃ hiṃsāṃ paradārābhimarśanam garvaṃ dambhaṃ bhūtaviṣavyādhitantraṃ nacācaret / svaṃ mantramakṣasūtraṃ ca vidyāṃ jñānasvarūpakam samācārānguṇānkleśānsiddhiliṅgāni gūhayet / guruṃ śāstraṃ devavahnī jñānavṛddhāṃstriyo vratam guruvargaṃ yathāśaktyā pūjayedaṣṭakaṃ tvidam / dīnānkliṣṭānpitṝnkṣetrapālānprāṇigaṇān khagān śmāśānikaṃ bhūtagaṇaṃ dehadevīśca tarpayet / śivaṃ śaktiṃ tathātmānaṃ mudrāṃ mantrasvarūpakam saṃsārabhuktimuktīśca guruvaktrāttu bhāvayet / rāgaṃ dveṣamasūyāṃ ca saṃkocerṣyābhimānitāḥ samayapratibhettṝṃstadanācārāṃśca ghātayet / paśumārgasthitānkrūrāndveṣiṇaḥ piśunāñjaḍān

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v531] One should delude the king's evil attendants and those who create obstacles, and one should worship the shakinis, who are described in this way in the revered scripture.

[tal-a15-v532] The shakinis have twofold boldness, fourfold desire, and eightfold greed; therefore they are to be feared. That is enough to say.

[tal-a15-v533] Those who claim to stand in the kula tradition but remain outside the heroic substances should not be lived with; the revered Madhava Kula says one must not dwell together with such bound ones.

[tal-a15-v534] One should always worship the circle of deities, the guru, the fire, and the scripture as equal, and should not eat anything at all that has not first been offered to them.

[tal-a15-v535] One should not take the guru's property and should honor the guru's circle; that circle is to be regarded, through knowledge, as like his brother, wife, and children.

[tal-a15-v536] That relation is not based on birth or worldly ties, for such a person remains bound; instead, one's attachment should serve the accomplishment of worship of the guru.

[tal-a15-v537] The guru's group should not be worshipped for its own greatness but honored like the guru; one must not criticize the guru or give any reason for such criticism.

[tal-a15-v538] One should not listen to criticism of the guru, should not anger him, and should not do anything in his presence without permission, except serving him.

[tal-a15-v539] Worldly and non-worldly duties, anger, play, austerity, recitation, and anything used by the guru—such as his bed, clothes, or seat—are all subject to strict restraint.

[tal-a15-v540] One should not use what the guru has used and should not touch it with the feet; instead one should honor it. The revered Traishirasa says that violations call for expiations such as krcchra and candrayana.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-rājñaścānucarānpāpānvighnakartṝṃśca mohayet / śākinyaḥ pūjanīyāśca tāścetthaṃ śrīgamoditāḥ sāhasaṃ dviguṇaṃ yāsāṃ kāmaścaiva caturguṇaḥ / lobhaścāṣṭaguṇastāsāṃ śaṅkyaṃ śākinya ityalam kulāmnāyasthitā vīradravyabāhyāstu ye na taiḥ / paśubhiḥ saha vastavyamiti śrīmādhave kule devatācakragurvagniśāstraṃ sāmyātsadārcayet / aniveditametebhyo na kiṃcidapi bhakṣayet etaddravyaṃ nāpaharedguruvargaṃ prapūjayet / sa ca tadbhrātṛbhāryātukprāyo vidyākṛto bhavet na yonisaṃbandhakṛto laukikaḥ sa paśuryataḥ / tasyābhiṣvaṅgabhūmistu gurvārādhanasiddhaye arcyo na svamahimnā tu tadvargo guruvatpunaḥ / gurornindāṃ na kurvīta tasyai hetuṃ nacācaret naca tāṃ śṛṇuyānnainaṃ kopayennāgrato@sya ca / vinājñayā prakurvīta kiṃcittatsevanādṛte laukikālaukikaṃ kṛtyaṃ krodhaṃ krīḍāṃ tapo japam / gurūpabhuktaṃ yatkiṃcicchayyāvastrāsanādikam nopabhuñjīta tatpadbhyāṃ na spṛśetkiṃtu vandayet / śrīmattraiśirase@pyuktaṃ kṛcchracāndrāyaṇādibhiḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v541] Even if someone stands in the forest like a log, follows the razor-edge vow, and is firmly established in restraints and observances, he still does not attain the supreme state.

[tal-a15-v542] But one who is devoted to worship of the guru in thought, action, and speech obtains from the pleased guru the full and greatly wondrous highest good.

[tal-a15-v543] Just as the earth, covered on all sides by falling snow, becomes hard like stone through contact with the wind and remains so, so too a certain state becomes fixed.

[tal-a15-v544] In restraints and the like, when one becomes immobile, only a limited state is grasped, like that hardened snow; but from a properly worshipped guru one obtains full, expanding knowledge.

[tal-a15-v545] Consciousness is present everywhere and abides in the knowable; the teaching of one who knows this can immediately lift one upward. Therefore one should worship the guru.

[tal-a15-v546] The revered Sara says that even conversation with such a guru destroys sin in an instant; therefore one should examine a guru carefully, using scriptural teaching and the signs of true knowledge.

[tal-a15-v547] Live according to scriptural conduct and associate with the guru in that way. He may sometimes teach out of affection, but he cannot be won over by greed.

[tal-a15-v548] When the guru is pleased, the gods and ancestors are satisfied; beings cross beyond the hells and go immediately to the great city of Shiva.

[tal-a15-v549] The house where the guru eats or stays is said to reach Shiva's city; knowing this, one should always worship one's own guru in the ancestral shraddha rite.

[tal-a15-v550] The guru himself should eat and direct others for that purpose; an initiated disciple should not perform the shraddha and similar rites independently.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-araṇye kāṣṭhavattiṣṭhedasidhārāvrato@pi san / niyamastho yamastho@pi tatpadaṃ nāśnute param gurvārādhanasaktastu manasā karmaṇā girā / prāpnoti gurutastuṣṭāt pūrṇaṃ śreyo mahādbhutam himapātairyathā bhūmiśchāditā sā samantataḥ / mārutaśleṣasaṃyogādaśmavattiṣṭhate sadā yamādau niścale tadvadbhāva ekastu gṛhyate / gurostvārādhitātpūrṇaṃ prasarajjñānamāpyate sarvato@vasthitaṃ cittvaṃ jñeyasthaṃ yasya tatkathā / sadya eva nayedūrdhvaṃ tasmādārādhayedgurum śrīsāre@pyasya saṃbhāṣātpātakaṃ naśyati kṣaṇāt / tasmātparīkṣya yatnena śāstroktyā jñānalakṣaṇaiḥ śāstrācāreṇa varteta tena saṅgaṃ tathā kuru / snehājjātu vadejjñānaṃ lobhānna hriyate hi saḥ tena tuṣṭena tṛpyanti devāḥ pitara evaca / uttīrya narakādyānti sadyaḥ śivapuraṃ mahat bhuṅkte tiṣṭhedyatra gṛhe vrajecchivapuraṃ tu saḥ / iti jñātvā sadā pitrye śrāddhe svaṃ gurumarcayet bhuñjīta sa svayaṃ cānyānādiśettatkṛte guruḥ / yo dīkṣitastu śrāddhādau svatantraṃ vidhimācaret

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v551] If he acts independently, everything becomes fruitless and the pledge is transgressed; one should also avoid substances offered in the Saiddhantika way or fit for Chandi.

[tal-a15-v552] One should never utter a word that names a shakini; women are to be honored, even if they are unattractive, old, or earn their living by a craft.

[tal-a15-v553] Women of the lowest caste, women with deformed limbs, courtesans, and women who act freely are to be honored with effort, as declared in the revered scripture.

[tal-a15-v554] They are without conventional conduct, eat all things, are beyond right and wrong, move by their own will, eat meat, and are unrestrained; they are like goddesses.

[tal-a15-v555] Courtesans and their houses are to be honored, and there one should worship the ritual sequence as at a sacred confluence; one must not do anything toward women that would make them feel disgust.

[tal-a15-v556] Therefore, one should not look at them naked or with breasts exposed; and even if an old woman is present, one should not feel disgust at her mudrikā.

[tal-a15-v557] At the gathering one should not display deformity or beauty; one should worship an empty-bodied deity image at crossroads and similar places.

[tal-a15-v558] On all festivals, ordinary and special, worship should be performed; there is no break in observance toward the guru, and greed must be avoided in the gathering.

[tal-a15-v559] One should never feel disgust toward wine and other vīra substances, nor criticize them; rather, one should always honor those who partake of them.

[tal-a15-v560] For the sake of instruction, faults may be pointed out, but one must not hate in one's heart; instead, one should strive to uproot alien conceptions.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tasya tanniṣphalaṃ sarvaṃ samayena ca laṅghyate / saiddhāntikārpitaṃ caṇḍīyogyaṃ dravyaṃ vivarjayet śākinīvācakaṃ śabdaṃ na kadācitsamuccaret / striyaḥ pūjyā virūpāstu vṛddhāḥ śilpopajīvikāḥ antyā vikāritāṅgyaśca veśyāḥ svacchandaceṣṭitāḥ / tathāca śrīgame proktaṃ pūjanīyāḥ prayatnataḥ nirācārāḥ sarvabhakṣyā dharmādharmavivarjitāḥ / svacchandagāḥ palāśinyo lampaṭā devatā iva veśyāḥ pūjyāstadgṛhaṃ ca prayāgo@tra yajetkramam / strīṣu tannācaretkicidyena tābhyo jugupsate ato na nagnāstāḥ paśyennacāpi prakaṭastanīḥ / vṛddhāyāḥ saṃsthitāyā vā na jugupseta mudrikām vaikṛtyaṃ tatra saurūpyaṃ melakaṃ na prakāśayet / devamūrtiṃ śūnyatanuṃ pūjayettripathādiṣu sarvaparvasu sāmānyaviśeṣeṣu viśeṣataḥ / pūjā guroranadhyāyo melake lobhavarjanam na jugupseta madyādi vīradravyaṃ kadācana / na nindedatha vandeta nityaṃ tajjoṣiṇastathā upadeśāya na doṣā hṛdayaṃ cenna vidviṣet / vijātīyavikalpāṃśotpuṃsanāya yateta ca

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v561] The names of the guru, the scripture, and the goddesses should not be uttered casually in mantra outside of worship; when properly invoked, they should then be satisfied.

[tal-a15-v562] One should not perform tarpaṇa for a mantra that has merely arrived, because it takes away half of one's body; so the Blessed Lord declared.

[tal-a15-v563] In the revered Ūrmi scripture it is taught that one must not publicize the conduct of goddesses and vīras, must not feel disgust toward it, and must not speak without the ritual substance in hand.

[tal-a15-v564] One should speak the guru's name preceded by śrī, especially when holding an offering; one must not step over the shadow of the guru and other revered figures, and one must not associate with sectarian rivals.

[tal-a15-v565] When talking, one may explain the meaning of one's own scripture, but should not speak otherwise or give hints. In an occasional rite, one should not add special worship beyond the daily worship.

[tal-a15-v566] In the middle of the year, and especially during the pavitraka rite, one devoted to another mantra should not take part, and another scripture should not be followed.

[tal-a15-v567] Knowledge that is not firmly rooted can be shaken by the views of others. Household implements and weapons should be honored through fire and offering.

[tal-a15-v568] One should not touch or step over worshipful things with the feet. When the guru and his group come to the house, one should show them some special honor.

[tal-a15-v569] One should not criticize initiated people out of hostility. If correction is given for instruction and without hostility, it is not a fault.

[tal-a15-v570] One should not live closely with those who hold lower views, such as Vaishnavas and others. One should not eat or sleep with them, nor reveal one's own spiritual state to them.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-guroḥ śāstrasya devīnāṃ nāma mantre yatastataḥ / arcāto@nyatra noccāryamāhūtaṃ tarpayettataḥ āgatasya ca mantrasya na kuryāttarpaṇaṃ yadi / haratyardhaśarīraṃ tadityūce bhagavānyataḥ śrīmadūrmau ca devīnāṃ vīrāṇāṃ ceṣṭitaṃ na vai / prathayenna jugupseta vadennādravyapāṇikaḥ śrīpūrvaṃ nāma vaktavyaṃ gurordravyakareṇa ca / gurvādīnāṃ na laṅghyā ca chāyā na tairthikaiḥ saha jalpaṃ kurvansvaśāstrārthaṃ vadennāpica sūcayet / nityādviśeṣapūjāṃ ca kuryānnaimittike vidhau tato@pi madhye varṣasya tato@pi hi pavitrake / anyastamantro nāsīta sevyaṃ śāstrāntaraṃ ca no aprarūḍhaṃ hi vijñānaṃ kampetetarabhāvanāt / gṛhopaskaraṇāstrāṇi davatāyāgayogataḥ arcyānīti na padbhyāṃ vai spṛśennāpi vilaṅghyet / guruvarge gṛhāyāte viśeṣaṃ kaṃcidācaret dīkṣitānāṃ na nindādi kuryādvidveṣapūrvakam / upadeśāya no doṣaḥ sa hyavidveṣapūrvakaḥ na vaṣṇavādikādhaḥsthadṛṣṭibhiḥ saṃvasedalam / sahabhojanaśayyādyarnaiṣāṃ prakaṭayetsthitim

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v571] It is said in the revered Madhava lineage that one should always avoid Vedic and Vaishnava teachings, and whatever is spoken by those established in other systems.

[tal-a15-v572] Association with those of unworthy lineage brings the fear of falling from one's own lineage. Therefore, in the Kula tradition, especially where one vessel is shared, one should avoid them.

[tal-a15-v573] If, through carelessness, one forms a friendship in a gathering with a follower of another Agama, the revered Urma teaches that one should worship the circle.

[tal-a15-v574] One should not associate at all with someone who delights in another guru, is deluded, lives off the property of the gods, harms the shakti, or is corrupt.

[tal-a15-v575] One should not go to a shrine or similar place in initiation and related matters out of mere doubt. If the prescribed faith has become weak, one should not act on that basis.

[tal-a15-v576] One should not judge or speak of those in the teaching in terms of their former birth. One should deal with all simply as non-different from Shiva.

[tal-a15-v577] Sit with true knowledge, strive for illumination, and do not fall into uninitiated fruitlessness.

[tal-a15-v578] Night practice in the assembly center excludes ordinary people, and the devotee of the goddess does not smell burning meat.

[tal-a15-v579] Protecting the guru's command, one abandons mantra-identification and becomes equipped with scripture, worship, japa, meditation, and discernment.

[tal-a15-v580] Do not perform fruitless action, do not strive in threefold action, do not dispute through mantra and tantra, and do not eat poison.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-uktaṃ śrīṃmādhavakule śāsanāntarasaṃsthitān / vedoktiṃ vaiṣṇavoktiṃ ca tairuktaṃ varjayetsadā akulīneṣu saṃparkāttatkulātpatanādbhayam / ekapātre kulāmnāye tasmāttānparivarjayet pramādācca kṛte sakhye goṣṭhyāṃ cakraṃ tu pūjayet / śrīmadūrmau ca kathitamāgamāntarasevake gurvantararate mūḍhe devadravyopajīvake / śaktihiṃsākare duṣṭe saṃparkaṃ naiva kārayet na vikalpena dīkṣādau vrajedāyatanādikam / uktāsthāśithilatve yannimittaṃ naiva taccaret śāsanasthānpurājātyā na paśyennāpyudīrayet / naca vyavaharetsarvāñchivābhedena kevalam sadvidyaiḥ sākamāsīta jñānadīptyai yateta ca / nāsaṃskṛtāṃ vrajettajjaṃ viphalatvaṃ nacānayet melakārdhaniśācaryā janavarjaṃ ca tannahi / māṃsādidāhagandhaṃ ca jighreddevīpriyo hyasau gurvājñāṃ pālayansarvaṃ tyajenmantramayo bhavet / śāstrapūjājapadhyānavivekatadupakriyāḥ akurvanniṣphalāṃ naiva ceṣṭeta trividhāṃ kriyām / mantratantrairna vādaṃ ca kuryānno bhakṣayedviṣam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v581] When pledges are breached, ask the guru in his presence, or another of his lineage in his absence.

[tal-a15-v582] Follow what he said without doubt and with effort, because the mind has been made one with scriptural awakening.

[tal-a15-v583] Shiva indeed is the guru; his word is truth, and humility toward the guru again serves Shiva's self-purification.

[tal-a15-v584] His satisfaction gives fruit to the disciple, since attainment depends on the guru, even in samaya, for the knowledge-bearer.

[tal-a15-v585] By great regard for that knowledge one knows the supreme guru; therefore, having obtained knowledge, one does not rely on external men.

[tal-a15-v586] He is not trusted in knowledge; indeed he is fallen, and a mind not trusted in knowledge is not established by mere words.

[tal-a15-v587] Never worship a knowledge-corrupter with the heart; such a person is not a guru, and even if made one, he should be abandoned.

[tal-a15-v588] With primary intellect one does not regard gurus among Vaishnavas and others as gurus; thus a qualification is stated in the named scripture.

[tal-a15-v589] The guru's command is not to be neglected in a life doubt; Kaula initiation and Kaula scripture reveal truth knowledge.

[tal-a15-v590] He by whom one is truly called guru is the guru; others are mere name-bearers, as the scripture states the qualification.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-samayānāṃ vilope ca guruṃ pṛcchedasannidhau / tadvargaṃ nijasantānamanyaṃ tasyāpyasaṃnidhau tenoktamanutiṣṭhecca nirvikalpaṃ prayatnataḥ / yataḥ śāstrādisaṃbodhatanmayīkṛtamānasaḥ śiva eva gururnāsya vāgasatyā viniḥsaret / śivasya svātmasaṃskṛtyai prahvībhāvo guroḥ punaḥ hlādāyetyubhayārthāya tattuṣṭiḥ phaladā śiśoḥ / gurvāyattaikasiddhirhisamayyapi vibodhabhāk tadbodhabahumānena vidyādgurutamaṃ gurum / ataḥ saṃprāpya vijñānaṃ yo gurau bāhyamānavān nāsau vijñānaviśvasto nāsatyaṃ bhraṣṭa eva saḥ / jñānānāśvastacittaṃ taṃ vacomātreṇa śāstritam bhaktaṃ ca nārcayejjātu hṛdā vijñānadūṣakam / tādṛk ca na guruḥ kāryastaṃ kṛtvāpi parityajet mukhyabuddhyā na saṃpaśyedvaiṣṇavādigatāngurūn / tathāca śrīmadūrmyākhye guroruktaṃ viśeṣaṇam gurvājñā prāṇasaṃdehe nopekṣyā no vikalpyate / kauladīkṣā kaulaśāstraṃ tattvajñānaṃ prakāśitam yenāsau gururityukto hyanye vai nāmadhāriṇaḥ / śrīmadānandaśāstre ca tathaivoktaṃ viśeṣaṇam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v591] Because initiation gives mantra scripture and truth knowledge, he is indeed the guru; the unmanifest linga stands, and no linga is held.

[tal-a15-v592] One should not equally mix conduct with linga-bearers; only the linga-bearer is to be protected, not treated with disgust, even if deformed.

[tal-a15-v593] In the Kula it is said that liberation comes from removing doubt; this impure dwelling and even news of liberation are rare.

[tal-a15-v594] Do not write the mantra heart; extract the mantra from its limb, but do not scratch it in writing.

[tal-a15-v595] Do not fixate on non-truth, and do not act from partiality toward knowers of birth, knowledge, family, conduct, body, place, quality, or meaning.

[tal-a15-v596] Quickly abandon the eight planets and non-planets shown in the cave, and likewise those shown as horse in the Nishichara beginning.

[tal-a15-v597] If I am a Brahmin, how can this birth-planet, which obstructs others, be performed beyond what Veda scripture says?

[tal-a15-v598] Thus others are also examples; by the Kula cave path, even the unwilling shows that form in non-that nature.

[tal-a15-v599] He here covers true form, like a planet as said; in the nature of consciousness there is no conception of birth and the like.

[tal-a15-v600] Form covers that form by true form; any conception sufficiently covers the indivisible self of the consciousness principle.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-yasmāddīkṣā mantraśāstraṃ tattvajñānaṃ sa vai guruḥ / tiṣṭhedavyaktaliṅgaśca na liṅgaṃ dhārayet kvacit na liṅgibhiḥ samaṃ kaiścitkuryādācāramelanam / kevalaṃ liṅginaḥ pālyā na bībhatsyā virūpakāḥ śrīmadrātrikule coktaṃ mokṣaḥ śaṅkāpahānitaḥ / aśuddhavāsasnayaiṣā mokṣavārtāpi durlabhā na likhenmantrahṛdayaṃ śrīmanmāloditaṃ kila / tadaṅgāduddharenmantraṃ natu lekhe vilekhayet atattve@bhiniveśaṃ ca na kuryātpakṣapātataḥ / jātividyākulācāradehadeśaguṇārthajān grahāngrahānivāṣṭau drāktyajedgahvararśitān / tathā śrīniśicārādau hayatvenopadarśitān brāhmaṇo@haṃ mayā vedaśāstroktādaparaṃ katham / anuṣṭheyamayaṃ jātigrahaḥ paranirodhakaḥ evamanye@pyudāhāryāḥ kulagahvaravartmanā / atatsvabhāve tādrūpyaṃ darśayannavaśe@pi yaḥ svarūpācchādakaḥ so@tra graho graha ivoditaḥ / saṃvitsvabhāve no jātiprabhṛtiḥ kāpi kalpanā rūpaṃ sā tvasvarūpeṇa tadrūpaṃ chādayatyalam / yā kācitkalpanā saṃvittattvasyākhaṇḍitātmanaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a15-v601] The supreme lord declared in the splendid Ananda scripture that all should abandon the contraction-causing graha-state.

[tal-a15-v602] There the independent lord Vama is not caused by purity; goddess satisfaction in sacrifice is not from blood, flesh, or purity arrangement.

[tal-a15-v603] Discussion should be done equally with twice-born and outcastes; even at its end, rays unchanged by that maker would arise from doubt as hell.

[tal-a15-v604] The body is all-god-filled in all beings; this is clearly determined by splendid Nakulesha and others.

[tal-a15-v605] The body itself is the shrine, not another; one should go to one tirtha, remember the mantra, and avoid other tirthas.

[tal-a15-v606] Having easily known this rite, one should abandon the rite-net; samadhi certainty is not obtained by another.

[tal-a15-v607] Thus thinking, the rite-knower should avoid delusion; besides the heart of the mantra, nothing else is supreme anywhere.

[tal-a15-v608] Thus thinking, the rite-knower should abandon the mantra-net; he should feed the offering and throw the river remainder in water.

[tal-a15-v609] When eaten by them, no fault would arise; water-born and previously initiated ones are protected by supremacy from contact.

[tal-a15-v610] These pledges are declared as means of knowledge attainment; thus proclaiming pledges, the teacher worships the god.
